records.title: Electric Power Steering (EPS) Assist Fault — Sudden Loss of Assist
records.description: Fiestas can display 'Power Steering Assist Fault — Service Required' and lose electric power-steering assist, sometimes intermittently while driving. Root causes include torque-sensor faults and intermittent electrical connections in the steering column/gear that stop the control module from commanding the assist motor. When assist drops out the wheel becomes very heavy (manual mode), and some owners report the wheel jerking or pulling; Ford's broader EPS defects have driven multiple recalls and legal actions across its lineup. This is a safety-relevant electrical/steering failure.
records.solution: Scan the EPS module for fault codes and check steering-column/gear connectors and the torque sensor for intermittent connections. Reseat/repair wiring and clear codes; if the fault persists, the steering gear or EPS motor/torque-sensor assembly typically needs replacement (or software update where a campaign applies). Verify any open Ford steering campaign by VIN.
symptoms: 'Power Steering Assist Fault' warning message
Steering suddenly heavy / loss of assist
Intermittent heavy steering while driving
Wheel jerk or pull
Assist restored after restart then recurs
Warning light on dash

records.title: Electronic Throttle Body Failure — Sudden Limp Mode & Wrench Light
records.description: The drive-by-wire electronic throttle body (ETB) develops an internal electronic/motor fault (not just dirt) that causes the powertrain control module to command reduced power. The car drops into limp mode with a wrench/powertrain-malfunction light, often storing throttle-position or actuator-control codes. Because the failure is internal to the unit, cleaning does not fix it. This is a recognized Ford-family ETB problem shared with Focus, Escape, Fusion and Transit Connect, and is reported by Fiesta owners including on the 1.6L engines.
records.solution: Replace the electronic throttle body with an updated OEM/Motorcraft unit and perform the throttle-relearn/idle-relearn procedure afterward to prevent high idle and drivability faults. Cleaning is not a durable fix once the internal fault is present.
symptoms: Sudden loss of power / limp mode while driving
Wrench (powertrain malfunction) warning light
Reduced or unresponsive acceleration
Rough or high idle
Intermittent stalling

records.title: Fiesta ST Rear Motor Mount (Dogbone) Bushing Failure — Vibration & Wheel Hop
records.description: The Fiesta ST's soft OEM rear motor mount (RMM / 'dogbone') bushing cannot withstand the 1.6L EcoBoost's torque and the high heat at its location, so the rubber degrades and allows excessive engine movement. This produces clunking on throttle on/off, driveline shudder, and wheel hop under hard acceleration, and accelerates wear on the remaining mounts. It is one of the most-discussed Fiesta ST maintenance items; owners commonly fit a polyurethane insert or an upgraded mount to eliminate the slop.
records.solution: Inspect the rear motor mount for torn/collapsed rubber and excessive engine rock. Install a polyurethane RMM insert or a stiffer upgraded rear motor mount to control engine movement; consider refreshing the full mount set if the others are also worn, since stiffening one loads the rest. Note added NVH is normal with stiffer bushings.
symptoms: Clunk/thunk on throttle on-off
Driveline shudder or vibration
Wheel hop under hard acceleration
Excessive engine rock when blipping throttle
Vibration felt through shifter/cabin
Notchy engagement of gears at low speed

records.title: Ignition Coil / Spark Plug Misfire — Oil-Fouled Coils & Water Ingress in Plug Wells
records.description: Fiestas — especially the 1.6L EcoBoost ST — commonly throw misfire codes and run rough at idle from failing ignition coils and fouled spark plugs. Owners report oil creeping onto the coil boots and, notably, rainwater entering the spark-plug wells via the washer-jet routing, which soaks the plugs/coils and causes cylinder-specific misfires. Direct-injection combustion also makes the EcoBoost more prone to a slightly lumpy cold idle. Left unaddressed, a persistent misfire can trigger limp mode.
records.solution: Read misfire codes to identify the cylinder. Inspect plug wells for water/oil intrusion; if water is present, seal the washer-jet path and dry the wells. Replace fouled spark plugs with the correct heat range and gap, and replace failed coils (clean oil-contaminated boots or replace). Fix any upstream oil leak so coils don't re-foul. Clear codes and road-test.
symptoms: Rough idle / shaking at idle
Cylinder-specific misfire code
Check-engine light flashing under misfire
Hesitation or stumble under load
Water or oil found in spark-plug wells
Occasional limp mode

records.title: Manual Transmission Clutch Judder & Slave/Release Cylinder Failure
records.description: Manual-transmission Fiestas (5-speed B5/IB5) commonly develop clutch judder, a soft/sinking pedal, and inability to select gears when the concentric slave/release cylinder or clutch master cylinder fails. Owners report the clutch going to the floor when stopped and gears becoming impossible to select, sometimes temporarily restored by restarting. Because the slave cylinder is inside the bellhousing, replacement requires removing the transaxle, so labor is significant. Contributing factors include worn or dislodged master-cylinder internals, contaminated hydraulic fluid, and normal clutch wear producing judder on take-up.
records.solution: Diagnose the hydraulic clutch: bleed and check for a firm pedal; if fluid loss or a sinking pedal is present, replace the concentric slave/release cylinder (transaxle out) and, when the box is out, replace the clutch disc, pressure plate, and release bearing as a set. Inspect/replace the clutch master cylinder and flush with correct-spec fluid. Address judder by replacing a glazed/contaminated clutch and checking engine/gearbox mounts.
symptoms: Clutch pedal sinks to floor / stays down
Judder or shudder when releasing the clutch
Difficulty or inability to select gears
Loss of clutch fluid
Grinding on gear engagement
Clutch bites very high or slips

records.title: Power Window Regulator / Cable Failure — Glass Drops Into Door
records.description: The plastic-geared window motor cog and the regulator's lift cables/clips wear or break, causing the window to fall inside the door, stick partway, or move only after repeated button presses. A characteristic symptom is a clicking/chattering or grinding noise as the glass jams or slips off its carrier. Commonly affects the driver's door (highest cycle count) but occurs on all doors, and the 3-door glass is frequently cited. Distinct from a purely electrical (switch/fuse) fault — the motor often runs while the glass does not move because the cable/cog has failed.
records.solution: Replace the window regulator assembly (regulator + motor as a unit is common); re-seat the glass on the carrier and verify the cables/clips. Where only the motor cog is stripped, a new motor/regulator cures it. Check the switch and one-touch initialization after repair.
symptoms: Window drops down inside the door
Glass sticks partway or needs repeated presses
Clicking, chattering or grinding from the door
Motor runs but glass does not move
Window moves crooked / off track

records.title: DPS6 PowerShift Dual-Clutch Transmission Shudder, Slipping, and Failure
records.description: The Ford Fiesta equipped with the DPS6 PowerShift dual-clutch automatic transmission is one of the most complained-about vehicles in recent history. The dry dual-clutch design causes severe shuddering, jerking, hesitation, and complete loss of power during acceleration. The clutch plates overheat and wear prematurely, often before 50,000 miles. The Transmission Control Module (TCM) software frequently fails to adapt properly, causing delayed shifts, harsh engagement, and rollback on hills. Ford faced a class-action lawsuit involving nearly 1.5 million vehicles and a federal settlement was reached.
records.solution: Check if your vehicle is covered under Ford's extended warranty or class-action settlement — many Fiestas qualify for free clutch and TCM replacement. If out of warranty, have the clutch assembly and TCM reprogrammed or replaced ($1,500-$3,500). Some owners have had success with multiple TCM reflashes to improve shift quality. As a last resort, some owners have converted to a manual transmission. Avoid the PowerShift entirely when purchasing a used Fiesta — manual transmission models are far more reliable.
symptoms: Violent shuddering or bucking during acceleration from a stop
Transmission slipping and RPMs flaring without acceleration
Harsh or jerky shifts between 1st and 2nd gear
Hesitation or delayed engagement when pressing the gas pedal
Vehicle rolls backward on hills even with foot on gas
Grinding or chattering noise from transmission area
Wrench warning light or transmission malfunction message

citations.title: Ford Program 14M02 - DPS6 TCM Extended Coverage
Ford DPS6 TCM Coverage and Documented Failure Symptoms

fixParts.note: ZF Services K70564-01. Fitment confirmed against the ShowMeTheParts catalog for this vehicle's year and engine.
fixParts.provenance: ShowMeTheParts fitment lookup by year and engine; buy links verified to carry the part number on a matching brand

records.title: EVAP Canister Purge Valve Failure
records.description: The EVAP canister purge valve sticks open, causing difficulty fueling (pump nozzle keeps clicking off), rough idle, and check engine light. Very common on the 1.6L engine.
records.solution: Replace the canister purge valve (solenoid). Clear codes and verify repair. Check EVAP hoses for cracks.
symptoms: Gas pump nozzle clicks off repeatedly
Rough idle after fueling
Check engine light
Fuel smell

records.title: Rear Suspension Knock — Worn Rear Shock Top Mounts & Damper Bushings
records.description: Fiestas (2008–2019, including ST) frequently develop knocking, clunking, or scrubbing noises from the rear suspension over bumps. Common causes are worn rear shock-absorber top mounts, deteriorated damper eye/lower-mount bushings, and torn rubber that lets the shock move in its mount. Owners also find rattling heat shields and, occasionally, a broken coil-spring fragment knocking in the lower mount. It is a wear-and-tear NVH issue rather than a catastrophic failure, but it is one of the most-searched Fiesta annoyances.
records.solution: Inspect the rear shocks for oil leaks, torn/perished top-mount and eye bushings, and play in the mount. Replace worn rear shock absorbers (typically in pairs) along with their top mounts and bushings. Check for a cracked coil spring and loose/rattling rear heat shields, and re-secure or replace as needed.
symptoms: Knocking or clunking over bumps from the rear
Scrubbing/squeaking rear-end noise
Rattle from rear on rough roads
Excess rear-end body movement
Oil film on rear shock body
Noise worse over speed bumps

records.title: SYNC / APIM Infotainment Freezing, Rebooting & Bluetooth/CarPlay Dropouts
records.description: Fiesta SYNC/MyFord Touch and SYNC 3 systems commonly freeze, randomly reboot, drop Bluetooth pairing, and lose Apple CarPlay connectivity. Many failures are software 'handshake' hangs, but a subset are hardware failures of the Accessory Protocol Interface Module (APIM), which can enter a 'zombie' state where it draws power but the UI is frozen and soft resets do nothing. Symptoms include black screens, disappearing menus, unresponsive buttons, and USB ports that stop charging. A physical APIM fuse-pull/hard reboot resolves most connectivity hangs; persistent freezing points to APIM hardware or corrupted firmware.
records.solution: First perform a SYNC soft reset (hold Power + Seek-Right until reboot) and a master reset to clear corrupt Bluetooth profiles. Update SYNC firmware via USB with Ford's official update. For a frozen/zombie module, do a hardware reboot by pulling the APIM fuse. If freezing, black screens, or dead USB ports persist, replace/reflash the APIM module at a dealer.
symptoms: Touchscreen freezes or goes black
System randomly reboots
Bluetooth won't pair or drops calls/audio
Apple CarPlay freezes or disconnects
Unresponsive menu buttons
USB ports stop charging

records.title: In-Tank Fuel Pump Failure — Stall Without Warning (Recall 15V005000)
records.description: Improper nickel plating of internal components in the Bosch in-tank fuel pump can cause the pump to fail, letting the engine stall without warning and increasing crash risk. Ford issued NHTSA recall 15V005000 covering certain 2014-2015 Fiesta (and related Fusion/MKZ) vehicles built spring 2014; the recall was first announced January 2015 and later expanded April 30, 2015. Owners report intermittent no-start and stalling. Outside the recall window, general in-tank pump wear produces similar hot-restart/low-pressure symptoms.
records.solution: For affected VINs, Ford dealers replace the fuel pump free of charge under recall 15V005000 — verify the VIN via NHTSA/Ford lookup. For out-of-recall failures, replace the in-tank pump module and check the fuel pump driver module (FPDM) where fitted. Confirm fuel-rail pressure after repair.
symptoms: Engine stalls without warning while driving
Intermittent no-start (often restarts after cooldown)
Long crank / hard start
Loss of power / sputtering under load

records.title: TDCi Diesel DPF Blockage & Failed Regeneration (Short-Trip Use)
records.description: Diesel Fiestas frequently suffer diesel particulate filter (DPF) blockage and incomplete/failed regeneration, especially on cars used mainly for short, low-speed journeys that never reach regeneration temperature. Soot accumulates, the DPF warning light appears, and the car may enter limp mode or dump excess fuel into the oil during failed active regens (raising oil level and diluting it). Underlying triggers are often other faults — a leaking/faulty injector, stuck EGR, blocked intake, or failed DPF differential-pressure/EGT sensor — so the blocked DPF is frequently a symptom rather than the root cause.
records.solution: When the DPF light shows, drive at a steady 40+ mph for ~20 minutes to allow passive/active regeneration before it fully blocks. If blocked, run a forced regeneration and diagnose the root cause: test the DPF pressure and EGT sensors, check EGR operation, and inspect for a leaking injector causing oil dilution. Clean or replace the DPF if soot loading is beyond limits, and change oil if fuel-diluted.
symptoms: DPF / exhaust warning light
Limp mode / reduced power
Frequent regeneration attempts
Rising engine oil level (fuel dilution)
Excess smoke or smell
Poor fuel economy after failed regen

records.title: Water Leak Into Footwell — Blocked Scuttle Drain / Pollen-Filter Housing
records.description: Fiestas commonly get wet passenger (and sometimes driver) footwell carpets from rainwater entering via the scuttle panel at the base of the windscreen. Leaves and debris block the scuttle drain, or the scuttle-to-windscreen seal fails, letting water pool and overflow into the cabin heater/pollen-filter housing and down into the footwell. The soaked carpet can cause musty smells, foggy windows, and electrical corrosion in floor connectors. It affects multiple generations and is a top owner complaint.
records.solution: Clear leaves/soil from the scuttle drain flaps and drainage channels, and reseal the scuttle panel to the windscreen where the seal has failed. Confirm the pollen/cabin-filter housing is sealed and draining. Dry the carpet fully (lift carpet, extract water, dehumidify) and check floor electrical connectors for corrosion.
symptoms: Wet passenger footwell carpet
Musty / damp smell in cabin
Windows fogging up
Water sloshing sound behind dash
Water dripping from under glovebox
Corroded floor electrical connectors

records.title: Wet Belt (Belt-in-Oil) Timing Belt Degradation Clogging Oil Pump Pickup
records.description: The 1.0L EcoBoost uses a 'wet' timing belt that runs submerged in engine oil. When oil is old, over-extended, or not to Ford's WSS-M2C948-B spec, the belt's rubber breaks down and delaminates ('pilling'). Shed fragments migrate through the sump and clog the oil pump pickup screen, causing loss of oil pressure and catastrophic engine failure. NHTSA opened an investigation after dozens of complaints of low oil pressure followed by power loss on 1.0L EcoBoost vehicles. Ford originally quoted a very long belt interval (10 yr / 150k mi) but real-world failures pushed independent shops to recommend ~6 yr / 60k mi replacement. Failure can also destroy the belt-driven oil pump and cause the crank pulley to shed the belt.
records.solution: Replace the wet timing belt on a shortened interval (roughly every 6 years / 60,000 miles), and always use only the Ford-specified low-additive oil. At belt replacement, drop the sump and clean/replace the oil pump pickup screen and inspect for rubber debris. If low oil pressure or belt debris is found, replace the oil pump and pickup and flush the system; severe cases with bearing damage need engine replacement.
symptoms: Oil pressure warning light
Loss of engine power / stalling
Rattling or ticking timing noise
Oil contaminated with rubber flakes
Engine seizure in severe cases
Rough running before failure

records.title: Lower Control Arm Ball Joint Failure
records.description: The Ford Five Hundred has a documented problem with premature lower control arm ball joint failure. The ball joints can wear and separate at relatively low mileage, causing the steering knuckle to disconnect from the control arm. In severe cases, the ball joint has sheared completely while driving at highway speeds, snapping the CV axle and causing a sudden loss of steering control. NHTSA received multiple complaints about this failure. The front suspension design carries heavy weight from the 3.0L V6 and front-wheel-drive transaxle, putting excessive stress on the ball joints.
records.solution: Have the lower ball joints inspected at every tire rotation or oil change. If any play is detected, replace both lower ball joints immediately ($300-$600 for both sides). Use quality aftermarket ball joints from Moog or similar — the OEM parts are undersized for the application. After replacement, get a full alignment. If the ball joint is making clunking noises, do NOT delay repair — a ball joint separation at speed is extremely dangerous.
symptoms: Clunking noise from front suspension over bumps
Steering wheel vibration at highway speed
Vehicle pulls to one side during braking
Uneven tire wear on front tires
Visible play when lifting the front wheel and checking for movement

records.title: CVT Transmission Shuddering, Slipping, and Premature Failure
records.description: The Ford Five Hundred equipped with the CVT (Continuously Variable Transmission) suffers from chronic shuddering, slipping, and premature failure. The CVT transmission bucks and shakes when decelerating or accelerating around 25 MPH, and the problem worsens as the transmission heats up. Many owners report the transmission slipping under acceleration, loss of reverse gear, and complete transmission failure at 80,000-120,000 miles. The CVT was supplied by ZF and proved unreliable in the Five Hundred application. Cold weather exacerbates the issues, with the CVT fluid thickening and causing delayed engagement and sluggish acceleration. Replacement transmissions are difficult to source as the supplier no longer manufactures new units.
records.solution: Change the CVT fluid every 30,000 miles using the correct CVT-specific fluid (NOT standard ATF). Have the speed sensors and solenoids tested if shuddering occurs — replacing a $100 sensor is preferable to a $5,000 transmission. If the transmission fails, rebuilt CVT units are available from specialty transmission shops for $3,000-$4,500 installed. Some owners have converted to a conventional 6-speed automatic from a Ford Taurus, though this requires significant modification ($3,000-$5,000).
symptoms: Shuddering or bucking when accelerating or decelerating around 25 MPH
Transmission slipping — RPMs rise without corresponding acceleration
Delayed engagement when shifting from Park to Drive or Reverse
Loss of reverse gear while forward gears still work
Check engine light with transmission codes P0700 or P0701
Sluggish acceleration especially in cold weather
Whining noise from transmission area

records.title: Premature Power Steering Rack and Pump Failure
records.description: The Ford Five Hundred is prone to premature power steering system failure, including the power steering rack-and-pinion assembly and the power steering pump. Owners report loss of power steering assist, groaning noises when turning the wheel, and complete system failure at relatively low mileage (25,000-60,000 miles). The hydraulic power steering system was under-engineered for the vehicle's weight, and the factory-filled fluid was found to contribute to premature wear. Ford issued a TSB recommending a fluid change from the factory fill to Mercon V fluid, acknowledging the problem.
records.solution: Flush the power steering fluid and replace with Motorcraft Mercon V as recommended by the Ford TSB. If the pump is groaning, replace it before it fails completely ($200-$400 parts and labor). If the rack-and-pinion is leaking or steering is loose, replacement costs $500-$1,100. Have both components inspected whenever a power steering noise develops — catching a pump failure early prevents damage to the more expensive rack.
symptoms: Groaning or whining noise when turning the steering wheel
Steering becomes heavy or difficult to turn at low speeds
Power steering fluid level drops requiring frequent top-offs
Fluid leak from power steering rack or pump
Steering assist cuts out intermittently, especially when cold

records.title: Electronic Throttle Body Failure
records.description: The electronic throttle body sticks or fails, causing the engine to enter limp mode with reduced power. The throttle plate bore wears and allows the plate to stick. May trigger wrench warning light on the dash.
records.solution: Replace the electronic throttle body. Perform a throttle body relearn procedure after installation. Clean the throttle body bore if symptoms are mild.
symptoms: Wrench warning light
Reduced power/limp mode
Rough idle
Hesitation on acceleration

records.title: Front Wheel Bearing Hub Assembly Failure
records.description: The front wheel bearing hub assemblies fail, causing a droning/humming noise that increases with speed. The bearing is integrated into the hub assembly and cannot be pressed separately. Common on AWD models.
records.solution: Replace the hub and bearing assembly. The ABS sensor is integrated, so the tone ring alignment is automatic with a new assembly. Torque the axle nut to 233 ft-lbs.
symptoms: Humming noise increases with speed
Noise changes when turning
ABS light on
Wheel play detected

records.title: Brake Booster Check Valve Failure
records.description: The brake booster check valve fails, allowing vacuum to leak and causing a hard brake pedal and longer stopping distances. Some owners report a hissing sound from the brake area when pressing the pedal.
records.solution: Replace the brake booster check valve and grommet. Test vacuum at the booster — should hold 15+ inches of vacuum. If the booster diaphragm is damaged, the entire booster needs replacement.
symptoms: Hard brake pedal
Hissing from brake area
Longer stopping distance
Engine idle changes when braking

records.title: Door Ajar Warning Stays On
records.description: The door ajar warning stays illuminated even with all doors closed, draining the battery if interior lights stay on overnight. Caused by faulty door latch switches that corrode or stick.
records.solution: Spray electrical contact cleaner into the door latch mechanism. Replace the door latch assembly if cleaning doesn't resolve it. Check each door individually to identify which sensor is faulty.
symptoms: Door ajar warning on with doors closed
Interior lights stay on
Battery drain overnight
Dome light won't turn off

records.title: Electric Power Steering (EPS) Failure and Assist Loss
records.description: The 2009-2013 Ford Flex uses an electric power steering system that is prone to sudden failure, leaving the driver with extremely heavy steering that requires significant effort to turn. The power steering control module can overheat or fail internally, and the steering motor itself can burn out. The failure often occurs without warning, typically during low-speed maneuvers like parking lot turns. This was one of the top NHTSA complaint categories for the Flex.
records.solution: Have the power steering control module and motor tested at a Ford dealer or independent shop with Ford-specific scan tools. The steering column assembly with motor costs $400-$800 for the part, plus $300-$500 labor. Some owners have had success with aftermarket rebuilt units for $200-$400. Ford issued a TSB with a software update that can help in some cases — ask the dealer to check for applicable TSBs.
symptoms: Steering suddenly becomes very heavy and difficult to turn
Power steering warning light illuminates on dashboard
Steering assist intermittently cuts in and out
Grinding or whining noise from the steering column
Steering feels normal at highway speed but fails at low speed

records.title: Power Transfer Unit (PTU) Seal Leaks and AWD System Failure
records.description: AWD-equipped Ford Flex models suffer from chronic Power Transfer Unit (PTU) seal leaks and eventual PTU failure. The PTU transfers power from the transaxle to the rear driveshaft and is sealed with halfshaft seals that deteriorate over time. When the seals leak, the PTU fluid level drops, causing the unit to overheat and produce metal shavings that destroy the internal gears. Ford issued a TSB acknowledging the problem but never recalled the part. The PTU has no dipstick and the fluid is considered "lifetime" by Ford, meaning most owners never check or change it — leading to premature failure.
records.solution: Change the PTU fluid every 30,000-40,000 miles regardless of Ford's "lifetime" fluid claim. Have a shop inspect the PTU seals at every oil change for leaks. If the PTU is leaking, replace the seals promptly ($300-$600) before the unit is damaged. If the PTU has already failed (grinding noise, AWD malfunction), replacement costs $1,200-$2,500. An independent transmission shop can flush the fluid at a fraction of the dealer cost.
symptoms: Brown or dark fluid leak near the front axle area
Burning oil smell from under the vehicle after driving
Grinding or whining noise from the front of the drivetrain
AWD malfunction warning light or message
Vibration at highway speeds from the drivetrain
Metal shavings or black sludge in PTU fluid

records.title: Internal Water Pump Failure Causes Coolant-Oil Mixing and Catastrophic Engine Damage
records.description: The 3.5L Duratec and 3.5L EcoBoost V6 engines in the Ford Flex have a critical design flaw: the water pump is driven by the timing chain and mounted internally inside the engine. When the water pump seal fails, coolant leaks directly into the engine oil, creating a milky sludge that destroys engine bearings in a matter of miles. Because the pump is internal, there is no external leak to warn the owner — the first symptom is often catastrophic engine failure. This is one of the most expensive and common failures on high-mileage Flex vehicles, with repair quotes ranging from $5,000 to $7,000+ for engine replacement.
records.solution: Proactively replace the water pump and timing chain as preventive maintenance between 100,000-120,000 miles ($1,500-$2,500 labor-intensive job). Check oil regularly for milky appearance or coolant smell — catching it early can save the engine. If coolant is found in the oil, stop driving immediately and have it towed. Use only Ford-approved coolant to minimize seal degradation. Consider extended warranty coverage when purchasing a high-mileage Flex.
symptoms: Milky or frothy substance on oil dipstick or under oil fill cap
Sweet smell from engine oil indicating coolant contamination
Coolant level dropping with no visible external leak
Engine overheating
Low oil pressure warning light
Knocking or ticking sound from engine indicating bearing damage
White or sweet-smelling exhaust

records.title: 2.0L Direct Injection Carbon Buildup on Intake Valves
records.description: The 2.0L GDI (Gasoline Direct Injection) and 2.0L EcoBoost engines in 2012-2018 Ford Focus accumulate carbon deposits on the intake valves over time because direct injection fuel never washes over the valve faces. Oil vapors from the PCV system coat the intake valves and harden into carbon deposits over 60,000-100,000 miles. As deposits build up, they restrict airflow, cause rough idle, misfires, and reduced power. This is a maintenance issue inherent to all direct-injection engines (BMW, VW, Ford, etc.) and is not covered under warranty except in severe cases. The only effective permanent repair is walnut blasting the intake valves.
records.solution: Walnut blasting (media blasting of intake valves with crushed walnut shells) is the most effective solution, costing $400-$800 at shops familiar with the procedure. DIY walnut blasting adapters for the 2.0L EcoBoost are available from US Vet Designs. Installing an oil catch can (PCV oil separator) on the intake tract reduces future buildup. Use top-tier gasoline (Chevron, Shell V-Power, Costco) which contains enhanced deposit control additives. Service interval: walnut blast every 40,000-60,000 miles.
symptoms: Rough idle, especially when cold
Misfires at idle or low load (P0300-P0304 codes)
Loss of power and throttle response, particularly at low RPM
Poor fuel economy (5-15% reduction)
Hesitation on light throttle application
Engine shaking or vibration at idle
Symptoms worsen progressively over many miles

records.title: Canister Purge Valve Failure Causing Rough Idle and Stalling
records.description: The 2012-2018 Ford Focus with the 2.0L GDI engine experiences frequent canister purge valve (CPV) failures that cause rough idle, stalling, difficulty starting (especially after refueling), and fuel-related DTCs. The purge valve sticks open, allowing fuel vapors to flood the intake manifold at inappropriate times. This is separate from the carbon buildup issue and is one of the most commonly replaced components on the 2012-2018 Focus. Ford issued TSBs addressing the issue and released updated purge valve designs. The problem affects both manual and automatic (PowerShift) transmission models. Focus Fanatics Forum documents this as one of the top five most-replaced parts on the Mk3 Focus.
records.solution: Replace the canister purge valve (Motorcraft CX-2571 or equivalent, $30-60 part). The valve is located on top of the engine near the intake manifold and is a 15-30 minute DIY job. Use the updated Ford part number to avoid repeat failures. Clear all stored codes after replacement and drive through one complete drive cycle to verify the fix. If codes P0452/P0453 persist after purge valve replacement, the fuel tank pressure sensor may also need replacement.
symptoms: Rough idle or engine surging at idle
Engine stalling after starting, especially after refueling
Difficulty starting the engine (extended crank time)
Check engine light with EVAP system codes
Fuel smell from engine bay
Hesitation during acceleration from a stop
Engine runs rich (black exhaust smoke)

records.title: Door Ajar Warning False Alarm and Interior Lights Staying On
records.description: The Focus door ajar switch integrated into the door latch assembly fails, causing the dash to display a door ajar warning when all doors are closed. This also keeps the interior dome lights on, which drains the battery overnight. The latch switch corrodes or wears out, sending a false open signal to the body control module. Any of the four doors can be affected, though the driver door is most common.
records.solution: Replace the door latch assembly containing the failed ajar switch. OEM latch assemblies cost $50-100; aftermarket versions are $30-60. Replacement takes 30-60 minutes and requires removing the door panel. As a temporary fix, the interior light fuse can be pulled to prevent battery drain, or the dome light switch can be set to the off position. Spraying WD-40 into the latch mechanism can temporarily restore the switch contact but is not a permanent fix.
symptoms: Door ajar warning on dash with all doors closed
Interior lights stay on after locking
Battery drain overnight
Door ajar chime sounds while driving
Alarm triggered by false door open signal

records.title: Side Door Latch Failure - Door Opening While Driving (Recall 16V643)
records.description: The 2012-2015 Ford Focus is included in Ford's massive door latch recall (16V643 / 14S17) covering 2.38 million vehicles. The pawl spring tab inside the side door latches can fracture, particularly in hot and humid climates. A fractured pawl spring tab causes the door to fail to properly latch, or to open unexpectedly while driving. Ford identified this as a safety defect after reports of accidents and injuries. All four door latches on affected vehicles may be defective. The condition is insidious because the door may appear to close normally while the latch pawl spring is already cracked.
records.solution: Ford Safety Recall 16V643 / 14S17 - dealers replace all affected side door latches at no charge, no mileage limit. Check safercar.gov or fordowner.com with VIN to verify recall status. Even if the car has changed ownership, recall repairs are always free regardless of current owner. Ford also issued subsequent recalls (16S30, 19V171) for additional vehicles with the same root cause.
symptoms: Door does not latch when attempting to close (bounces back)
Door ajar warning light on with door apparently shut
Door opens while vehicle is in motion
Unusual wind noise from a door that should be closed
Door latch sounds or feels different when closing

citations.title: NHTSA Focus Recall Results - Campaigns 16V643 and 20V331

records.title: DPS6 PowerShift Dual-Clutch Transmission Shudder, Hesitation, and Failure
records.description: The DPS6 PowerShift 6-speed dual-clutch automated transmission fitted to 2012-2018 Ford Focus (and 2011-2019 Fiesta) is widely considered one of the worst transmission designs in modern automotive history. The dry dual-clutch design was fundamentally unsuited for stop-and-go driving, producing violent shuddering during low-speed acceleration, hesitation when pulling away from stops, unexpected surging, and abrupt harsh shifts. Ford knew of the defects from the start but concealed them and continued selling vehicles. Multiple class action lawsuits resulted in settlements covering 2012-2016 models (expanded to 2017-2018). Ford issued dozens of TSBs and software reflashes that repeatedly failed to fix the underlying mechanical problem. The TCM (Transmission Control Module) failures are a distinct but related issue. Repair options include clutch replacement (temporary fix), TCM reprogramming, or complete transmission replacement.
records.solution: Check fordtransmissionsettlement.com for class action settlement eligibility. Ford's warranty extended to cover repeated repairs. Updated clutch service parts: Focus uses F1FZ-7B546-B clutch (replaces BV6Z-7B546-F). TCM repair/replacement per TSB 16-0109. Software recalibration via IDS tool at dealer. For definitive fix: remanufactured DPS6 transmission. Many owners chose to pursue buyback via state Lemon Laws. Latest settlements include 2017-2018 models under separate class action.
symptoms: Violent shuddering or juddering when accelerating from a stop
Transmission hesitates or refuses to move in Drive for 1-3 seconds
Unexpected lurch forward when releasing brakes at low speed
Grinding or clunking between gear changes
Transmission surging and jerking during low-speed driving
Vehicle bucks and shakes at 15-35 mph (clutch slip zone)
Transmission warning light or "Transmission Fault" message
Loss of drive in one or both gears
Delayed engagement from Park to Drive

citations.title: Ford Program 14M02 - DPS6 TCM Extended Coverage
Ford DPS6 TCM Coverage and Documented Failure Symptoms

records.title: Rear Wheel Bearing Premature Failure (1st-Generation Mk1/Mk1.5)
records.description: 1999-2007 Ford Focus (1st-generation Mk1 and Mk1.5) suffer from repeated rear wheel bearing failures, often within months of replacement. One Focus Fanatics owner reported the left rear wheel bearing failing 4 times in 7 months. Root cause is missing or degraded inboard spindle seals that allow brake dust and water into the bearing race, plus alignment drift (excessive negative camber or toe) accelerating wear. Ford acknowledged the seal design in owner communities but never issued a formal recall. Replacement requires the full hub assembly. The 2012-2018 Mk3 Focus has separate bearing issues with different root causes (not covered by this entry).
records.solution: Replace the rear wheel bearing/hub assembly as a complete unit - the bearing is sealed and non-serviceable. RepairPal estimates $317-429 per side. When replacing, clean the knuckle bore thoroughly and apply anti-seize compound to prevent the new bearing from seizing in the housing (makes future replacement much easier). If the vehicle is in a salt-belt state, replace both rear bearings simultaneously - the other side will likely fail soon after.
symptoms: Humming or growling noise from rear wheels that increases with speed
Rumbling noise that changes pitch when turning (load shifts off bearing)
Vibration felt through vehicle floor
Uneven rear tire wear
ABS warning light if bearing play affects wheel speed sensor
Loose or wobbly feeling in rear end
Grinding noise from rear at highway speeds

records.title: HVAC Blend Door Actuator Failure
records.description: The blend door actuator fails, causing the HVAC to blow only hot or only cold air regardless of temperature setting. A clicking noise behind the dash is the early warning sign.
records.solution: Replace the blend door actuator. Access requires removing part of the lower dash panel. The actuator is a small electric motor unit that clips onto the blend door shaft.
symptoms: Stuck on hot or cold air
Clicking behind dashboard
Temperature control unresponsive
Different temp from each vent

records.title: Ignition Coil Pack Failure
records.description: The coil-on-plug ignition coils on the 3.9L and 4.2L V6 engines fail frequently, causing misfires, rough running, and reduced fuel economy. Often one coil fails and the others follow shortly.
records.solution: Replace all six coil packs and spark plugs as a set for reliability. Use Motorcraft or quality aftermarket coils. Clear misfire codes after replacement.
symptoms: Engine misfire
Rough idle
Check engine light flashing
Poor fuel economy
Hesitation on acceleration

fixParts.note: Beck Arnley 178-8366. Fitment confirmed against the ShowMeTheParts catalog for this vehicle's year and engine.
fixParts.provenance: ShowMeTheParts fitment lookup by year and engine; buy links verified to carry the part number on a matching brand

records.title: Rear Axle Trailing Arm Bushing Deterioration
records.description: The Freestar's rear twist-beam axle trailing arm bushings crack and deteriorate, causing the rear end to feel loose and unstable. Worn bushings allow the rear axle to shift, causing poor alignment, inner tire wear, and a wandering feeling at highway speed.
records.solution: Replace both trailing arm bushings. Aftermarket polyurethane bushings last longer than OEM rubber. A rear alignment should be checked after bushing replacement to verify toe settings.
symptoms: Rear end feels loose or unstable
Inner rear tire wear
Wandering at highway speed
Clunking from rear over bumps
Rear end shifts during braking
Squeaking from rear suspension

records.title: AX4S Transmission Torque Converter Shudder and Failure
records.description: The Freestar's AX4S 4-speed automatic transmission develops torque converter shudder during light acceleration at 35-50 mph. The converter clutch lining disintegrates, contaminating the fluid with debris that damages the valve body and solenoids.
records.solution: A transmission fluid flush may resolve mild shudder. Severe cases require torque converter replacement and valve body cleaning. If the transmission has been slipping, a full rebuild is likely needed.
symptoms: Shudder at 35-50 mph during light acceleration
Transmission slipping
Harsh 3-4 shift
Delayed engagement from park
Check engine light with TCC code
Transmission fluid dark or burnt smelling

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 12V006 - Freestar Torque-Converter Output Shaft

records.title: Torque Converter Shudder and Transmission Failure
records.description: The Freestar inherited many of the Windstar transmission problems. The torque converter develops shudder during light acceleration, and the transmission can fail completely with forward clutch pack burn-up.
symptoms: Shuddering at 40-60 mph
Harsh shifts
Slipping
Transmission warning light

records.title: Alternator Failure and Battery Drain
records.description: The alternator fails prematurely on the 3.0L Duratec engine, often before 100,000 miles. The internal diode pack fails, which can also cause parasitic battery drain even when the vehicle is off.
records.solution: Replace the alternator. Test for parasitic draw after replacement to ensure the issue is fully resolved. Replace the serpentine belt if worn.
symptoms: Battery light on dashboard
Dead battery overnight
Dim headlights
Electrical accessories resetting

records.title: CVT Transmission Failure and Poor Acceleration
records.description: The Ford Freestyle shares the same problematic ZF CVT (Continuously Variable Transmission) as the Ford Five Hundred, and suffers from similar failure modes. The transmission develops poor acceleration, hesitation, stalling, and eventually complete failure, often around 80,000-120,000 miles. The CVT check engine light frequently illuminates as the transmission deteriorates. The manufacturer of the CVT no longer produces new units, making only rebuilt transmissions available at high cost. The Freestyle's heavier weight compared to the Five Hundred (due to its crossover body) puts even more stress on the CVT.
records.solution: Change CVT fluid every 30,000 miles with the correct CVT-specific fluid. If the transmission begins slipping or stalling, have speed sensors and solenoids tested first ($100-$300 for sensor replacement). For complete CVT failure, rebuilt units are available from specialty shops for $3,500-$5,500 installed. Some owners have opted to sell or trade the vehicle rather than invest in a CVT replacement, as the repair cost often exceeds the vehicle's value.
symptoms: Poor acceleration — vehicle feels sluggish and underpowered
Transmission hesitates or stumbles during acceleration
Check engine light illuminates with transmission codes
Vehicle stalls at low speed or when slowing down
Whining or droning noise from the transmission
Complete loss of drive — engine revs but vehicle does not move

records.title: Fuel System Issues and Stalling
records.description: The Ford Freestyle is prone to fuel system problems that cause stalling, rough running, and loss of power. Issues include failing fuel pumps, contaminated fuel injectors, and fuel pressure regulator failures. The 3.0L Duratec V6 can experience stalling during deceleration or while idling, particularly in hot weather. The fuel pump relay in the fuse box can also fail intermittently, cutting fuel delivery without warning. These problems often overlap with the throttle body and CVT issues, making diagnosis challenging.
records.solution: Have the fuel pressure tested under load — a weak fuel pump is the most common cause of stalling and should be replaced ($400-$700 including labor). Clean the fuel injectors with a professional cleaning service every 50,000 miles ($100-$200). Check the fuel pump relay in the fuse box if the vehicle stalls intermittently and restarts after sitting — a $10 relay swap can fix this. If the fuel pressure regulator is leaking (fuel smell from the engine bay), replace it ($150-$300).
symptoms: Engine stalls while decelerating or at idle
Difficulty starting the engine, especially when warm
Loss of power during acceleration
Rough idle with engine surging up and down
Fuel smell from the engine compartment

records.title: Power Steering Pump Whine and Leak
records.description: The power steering pump develops a loud whine and leaks fluid from the shaft seal or reservoir. Low fluid from the leak makes the whine worse and can lead to pump failure. Common after 60,000 miles.
records.solution: Replace the power steering pump and flush the system. Inspect all hoses and the steering rack for leaks. Use Mercon V as the power steering fluid per Ford spec.
symptoms: Whining noise when turning
Power steering fluid leak
Heavy steering
Groaning at full lock

fixParts.note: Cardone 20-323. Fitment confirmed against the ShowMeTheParts catalog for this vehicle's year and engine.
fixParts.provenance: ShowMeTheParts fitment lookup by year and engine; buy links verified to carry the part number on a matching brand

records.title: Throttle Body Malfunction and Unintended Forward Surge
records.description: The Ford Freestyle is subject to a significant safety issue where the vehicle surges or lunges forward unexpectedly at low speeds when in gear, even without the accelerator pedal being applied. The NHTSA investigated 238 complaints about this behavior, finding that a programming error in the engine computer causes the electronic throttle body to malfunction, particularly when the engine is under load from A/C operation, steering at full lock, or carrying heavy loads. In 18 reported cases, the surge caused accidents. Ford eventually issued a recall in December 2012 to reprogram the throttle body or replace it and reimburse owners who had already paid for the repair.
records.solution: Contact your Ford dealer to verify the throttle body recall has been completed on your vehicle. If not, Ford will reprogram the throttle body control module or replace the throttle body assembly free of charge. If you already paid for a throttle body repair before the recall, contact Ford for reimbursement. Until the recall is completed, be especially cautious when the A/C is running and the steering wheel is turned sharply — these are the most common conditions that trigger the surge.
symptoms: Vehicle lurches or surges forward at low speed without pressing the gas
Sudden unexpected acceleration while in a parking lot or at a stop
Surging is worse when the A/C is running
Surging occurs when the steering wheel is turned to full lock
Engine idles erratically or races when in gear
Check engine light with throttle position sensor codes

citations.title: NHTSA PE11-018 Closing Resume - Ford Freestyle Idle Instability
Ford Response and Testing in NHTSA PE11-018

records.title: 1.6L EcoBoost Localized Cylinder-Head Overheating and Engine Fire (Recall 14V437)
records.description: Early 1.6L EcoBoost Fusions can suffer a localized lack of coolant circulation that overheats one corner of the cylinder head; the head cracks and pushes oil/coolant onto the hot exhaust, and vehicle fires occurred while driving or after shutdown. Ford recall 14V437 covers 2013 Fusion 1.6L vehicles built in a defined window; the failure mode is distinct from the 1.5L coolant-into-cylinder intrusion issue.
records.solution: Under recall dealers inspect for coolant-system leaks and reprogram the PCM and instrument cluster with an updated overheat-detection/limp-home strategy; damaged engines are repaired as needed. Owners should never keep driving after a coolant-loss/overheat warning. A cracked head from overheating typically requires head or long-block replacement out of warranty.
symptoms: Coolant loss with no obvious external leak
Engine overheating / temperature warning
White exhaust smoke or misfire
Smell of burning oil, smoke from engine bay
Fire while driving or after shutdown

citations.title: NHTSA Fusion Recall Results - Campaigns 12V551 and 17V209

records.title: 1.5L EcoBoost Coolant Intrusion into Cylinders - Internal Engine Block Failure
records.description: The 1.5L EcoBoost in 2014-2019 Ford Fusion is affected by the same open-deck cylinder block design defect as the Escape. Coolant leaks internally from the block passages into the combustion chambers due to insufficient sealing surface and porous block material that cannot maintain coolant pressure over time. Ford extended warranty coverage to 7 years/84,000 miles for short block replacement per TSB 19-2139 and TSB 19-2375. A consolidated class action lawsuit covers 2013-2019 Fusion and Escape with 1.5L, 1.6L, and 2.0L EcoBoost engines. Some owners have experienced engine failure with no warning - no check engine light before coolant hydrolocked the cylinder.
records.solution: Ford TSBs 19-2139 and 19-2375 cover short block and head gasket replacement under extended warranty (7 years/84,000 miles from warranty start date). Verify coverage at fordowner.com or call Ford Customer Relations 1-800-392-3673. Class action lawsuit for out-of-warranty reimbursement: lieffcabraser.com/defect/ford-coolant. Post-repair: Ford recommends monitoring coolant level and using only Motorcraft Orange coolant (VC-3-B).
symptoms: White or gray smoke from exhaust, especially on cold starts
Engine misfires with P0300-P0303 codes (1.5L is 3 cylinders in newer versions; earlier is 4-cyl)
Coolant level dropping without visible external leak
Sweet smell from exhaust
Coolant reservoir bubbling or pressurizing excessively
Engine overheating
Rough idle that clears up as engine warms
No warning light in some cases before engine fails

records.title: 6F35 6-Speed Automatic Harsh/Delayed Shifting and Torque Converter Shudder
records.description: The 6F35 six-speed automatic is prone to harsh, banging, or delayed shifts (most often 2-3 and 3-4) plus a shudder/vibration when the torque converter clutch locks up at a steady 40-60 mph cruise. Root causes are worn valve-body separator-plate O-rings and bores that can no longer hold clean line pressure, clogged/worn shift solenoids, and torque-converter clutch degradation. Many units develop symptoms well before 100,000 miles. A 2019 class-action lawsuit accused Ford of concealing the 6F35 defect on Fusion and Escape.
records.solution: Start with a full fluid-and-filter service using the correct Mercon LV. For confirmed harsh shifts, reman or updated valve body with new solenoids is the durable fix; TCC shudder that survives a flush usually requires torque-converter replacement. Verify the transmission calibration is up to date (Ford released updated shift-strategy PCM/TCM reflashes). Severe internal wear = rebuild or reman transmission.
symptoms: Hard/banging upshifts especially 2nd-to-3rd
Shudder or vibration cruising at 40-60 mph
Delayed engagement into drive or reverse
Slipping or flaring between gears
Transmission overheating warning

records.title: AWD Power Transfer Unit (PTU) Overheating and Fluid Leak Failure
records.description: On AWD Fusions the Power Transfer Unit holds only about a quart of gear oil with no dipstick, service interval, or cooling, sitting next to hot exhaust and transaxle. The fluid cooks and breaks down, becoming thick, gummy, and black, and the seals leak. Owners report a burning smell in the cabin, whining/growling, and eventually PTU seizure that can damage the transmission. Failures often occur relatively early in the car's life.
records.solution: Preventive fluid changes roughly every 30,000 miles greatly extend PTU life even though Ford lists it as filled-for-life. A leaking unit may be resealed for $400-$600 if caught early; a failed PTU requires replacement, which dealers quote from ~$1,600 up to ~$3,100 including labor.
symptoms: Burning oil smell in cabin
Whining, growling, or grinding from center of vehicle
Brown/black fluid leak near transaxle/axle area
Vibration or shudder under acceleration
Loss of AWD function

records.title: Door Latch Pawl Spring Failure - Door Opens While Driving
records.description: The 2013-2016 Ford Fusion is subject to multiple door latch recalls due to the pawl spring tab inside the side door latches fracturing. The design is susceptible to failure in high-temperature and high-humidity climates. Over 90% of warranty claims occurred in hot/humid states. A fractured pawl spring tab causes the door to fail to latch properly, or to open unexpectedly while the vehicle is moving. Ford issued multiple recalls covering Fusion: the original 14S17, expanded with 16V643, and additional recalls covering 2014-2016 Fusion specifically. Ford and Lincoln recalled over 2 million vehicles total across multiple model lines for this defect.
records.solution: Ford Safety Recalls 14S17 / 16V643 / and subsequent recalls - dealers replace all affected side door latches at no charge. No mileage limit. Check safercar.gov or fordowner.com with VIN. The latches are replaced free regardless of current ownership. Multiple subsequent recalls covered additional years and models with the same issue.
symptoms: Door will not latch shut (bounces back when closed)
Door ajar warning chime or light with door apparently closed
Door opens while vehicle is moving
Wind noise from door area
Door latch mechanism feels loose or spongy

citations.title: NHTSA 2014 Fusion Recall Results - Door-Latch Campaigns
NHTSA 2016 Fusion Recall Results - Door-Latch Campaigns

records.title: Electronic Throttle Body Failure - Limp Mode and Wrench Light
records.description: The electronic throttle body suffers internal contamination/wear of the motor contacts, causing intermittent electrical failure rather than simple dirt buildup. The result is a sudden loss of power (limp/failsafe mode) with the amber wrench (powertrain) warning light, rough idle, or stalling, sometimes in traffic. Ford acknowledged the problem with extended-warranty program 13N03 for 2010-2013 models and Customer Satisfaction Program 16B32 for certain 2015-2016 vehicles including Fusion.
records.solution: For the limp-mode failure the throttle body must be replaced (cleaning does not fix internal electronic wear), followed by a mandatory throttle-body relearn to prevent high idle and driveability faults. Check whether the vehicle qualified for 13N03 or 16B32 coverage history.
symptoms: Wrench/powertrain warning light
Sudden loss of power / limp mode
Rough or surging idle
Stalling
Reduced throttle response

records.title: EVAP Purge Valve Stuck/Leaking - Check Engine Light and Rough Running
records.description: The under-hood evaporative-emissions purge valve on 2010-2011 Fusion/Milan (2.5L DOHC and 3.0L) built on or before 3/4/2011 can stick open or leak, unmetered vapor entering the intake. This lights the MIL and sets a cluster of EVAP and lean/fuel-trim codes, and can cause rough idle or hard starts. It is a documented Ford pattern failure with a related TSB covering the affected build range.
records.solution: Confirm the purge valve holds vacuum and clicks when energized; replace the stuck/leaking purge valve (inexpensive part). Verify no cracked EVAP hoses, a properly sealing gas cap, and an intact charcoal canister before clearing codes. Smoke-test the EVAP system if large-leak codes persist.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Rough idle or stalling
Hard start after refueling
Fuel smell
Failed emissions test

records.title: Front Brake Hose Rupture - Loss of Brake Fluid and Longer Stopping (Recall 23S12)
records.description: A design flaw in the front brake hoses lets them rupture over time, leaking brake fluid and increasing stopping distance. Ford recalled roughly 1.2-1.28 million Fusion and Lincoln MKZ sedans (recall 23S12) in 2023 after an NHTSA investigation. A ruptured hose causes a low brake-fluid warning, a change in pedal feel, and a real crash risk from degraded braking.
records.solution: Under recall 23S12 dealers replace both front brake hoses and, where equipped, modify the hose routing and ride-height sensor at no charge. Owners noticing a soft/low pedal or brake warning light should stop driving and have the hoses inspected immediately.
symptoms: Brake warning light on instrument cluster
Longer stopping distances
Soft, low, or changed brake pedal feel
Visible brake fluid leak at front wheels
Low brake fluid reservoir level

citations.title: Ford 23S12 Fusion Front Brake Hose Recall

records.title: HVAC Blend Door Actuator Failure - Clicking/Knocking Behind Dash, No Heat or AC
records.description: The plastic gears inside the HVAC blend-door actuator strip out, so the door can no longer move to route air correctly. The classic symptom is a repeated clicking or knocking noise from behind the dash (often at startup or when changing temperature), along with air stuck on one temperature, wrong vent output, or one side blowing hot while the other blows cold. It is one of the most common Fusion comfort complaints across all generations.
records.solution: Replace the failed blend-door actuator (driver side of the HVAC housing, accessed by dropping the glove box). After replacement, perform the actuator calibration: reconnect the battery, turn ignition to On without starting, and let the system self-learn its range for at least a minute. Parts are inexpensive; labor rises sharply if a deeper actuator requires dash removal.
symptoms: Repeated clicking/knocking noise behind dashboard
No heat or no cold air from vents
Temperature stuck on hot or cold
Different temperature from left vs right vents
Air blows from wrong vents

records.title: Hybrid High-Voltage Battery Degradation and Failure
records.description: Ford Fusion Hybrid spans two generations with different high-voltage batteries — degradation patterns differ. 1st-gen 2010-2012 (NiMH, ~1.4 kWh): typical degradation appears at 100,000-150,000 miles with reduced EV-mode range and increased ICE intervention. Replacement runs $2,500-$4,000 at independent hybrid specialists. 2nd-gen 2013-2020 (Lithium-ion, ~1.4 kWh): better thermal management has led to longer life on average but cell imbalance issues appear at 150,000+ miles. 'Stop Safely Now' warnings often precede full failure. 2013-2020 Energi PHEV variants share the architecture but with larger 7.6 kWh batteries — separate degradation curve. Owners should check cell balance via OBD-II scanner with hybrid module support (Forscan recommended).
records.solution: Check warranty first - Ford covers 8yr/100k miles (10yr/150k in CA, CT, MA, ME, MD, NJ, NY, OR, PA, RI, VT, WA states). If out of warranty, aftermarket/remanufactured battery packs from GreenTecAuto ($1,550-2,950 installed) are significantly cheaper than dealer replacement ($4,000-7,000). Individual cell replacement at specialized hybrid shops ($800-2,000) is an option if only specific cells have failed. Battery reconditioning is a temporary fix that may restore 60-80% of capacity for $300-800.
symptoms: Reduced electric-only driving range
Decreased fuel economy (gradual decline)
"Check Hybrid System" warning on dashboard
Slower-than-normal acceleration or power loss
Battery charge indicator drops faster than normal
Unusual noise from battery compartment area
Vehicle fails to start (complete battery failure)
Hybrid system shuts down and runs on gasoline only

citations.title: Ford TSB 20-2142 - Reduced Electric Vehicle Operation

records.title: MyFord Touch / SYNC 2 (APIM) Freezing, Black Screen, and Rebooting
records.description: The MyFord Touch / SYNC 2 system (driven by the APIM module) is widely reported to freeze, go black, reboot repeatedly, lose Bluetooth pairing, and drop audio or backup-camera display. The Accessory Protocol Interface Module (APIM) has a known tendency to fail, and Ford extended warranty coverage on the module for affected owners. Beyond annoyance, a blank screen can disable the backup camera and climate controls.
records.solution: Try a soft reset (hold Seek-up + Power until the screen goes black) and a Master Reset, then update SYNC software via USB. Persistent freezing/rebooting usually traces to a failing APIM, which is replaced and reprogrammed (as-built) at a dealer; check for any remaining extended-warranty coverage. Many owners retrofit later software or a replacement APIM.
symptoms: Touchscreen freezes or goes black
System reboots repeatedly while driving
Bluetooth/phone pairing failures
Backup camera image missing
Audio cuts out or controls unresponsive

records.title: Parasitic Battery Drain - Dead Battery / No Start (BCM & Modules)
records.description: Many Fusion owners report the battery going dead overnight or over a weekend from a parasitic draw. Common culprits are a module that fails to sleep - Body Control Module (BCM), APIM/infotainment, or amplifier - as well as the PATS anti-theft transceiver circuit on earlier cars. A healthy vehicle should draw under ~50mA at rest; failed modules keep the network awake and flatten the battery.
records.solution: Measure key-off current draw with a multimeter, then pull fuses one at a time until the draw drops to isolate the offending circuit/module. Repair or replace the module that will not sleep (commonly BCM, audio/APIM, or amplifier); reflash where required. Confirm the battery and alternator test good before condemning a module.
symptoms: Battery dead after sitting overnight or a weekend
Frequent jump-starts required
Clicking / no-crank no-start
Electrical gremlins or flickering
Short battery life

records.title: Electric Power Steering (EPS) Failure - Sudden Loss of Assist
records.description: 2014-2018 Ford Fusions use a different EPS module revision than the 2011-2013 recall (NHTSA 15V340) — but owners still report sudden loss of power steering assist, particularly at higher mileage. Without recall coverage, repairs are owner-paid: rack replacement typically $1,200-$2,000. Symptoms mirror the recalled generation (heavy steering, intermittent warnings, eventual full assist loss). For 2013 specifically, the 15V340 recall applies if the vehicle is without the 3.5L engine.
records.solution: Check safercar.gov with VIN for Recall 15V340/15S18 and 19V632 eligibility - free dealer repair. Out-of-recall: EPS rack assembly replacement ($1,200-$2,800). If experiencing intermittent "Service Power Steering" warning: try restarting vehicle as temporary workaround (does not fix underlying issue). Avoid car washes with high-pressure undercarriage spray aimed at steering gear area (accelerates bolt corrosion on 2013-2015 models).
symptoms: "Service Power Steering" warning message on instrument cluster
Sudden heavy steering requiring much more effort, especially at low speeds
Steering wheel becomes very difficult to turn
"Hill Assist Not Available" and "Service AdvanceTrac" warnings accompanying EPS failure
Intermittent loss of power steering that returns after restart
Complete steering assist loss at any speed
Grinding or clicking from steering column during turns

records.title: Power Window Regulator Failure and Window Bounce-Back
records.description: Gen-2 Fusions have a long-running window-module/regulator problem. A common 'bounce-back' fault makes the window roll up, hit the top, and immediately drop back down, and worn regulator gears/cables cause clicking, chattering, or grinding and can drop the glass inside the door. The driver-door switch and window-module re-initialization are frequently involved. Documented across 2013-2016 and beyond.
records.solution: Re-initialize (relearn) the auto up/down after battery or module work; if that fails, replace the affected window regulator (and motor) and, if the switch tests bad, the master window switch. Some cases require the window system re-initialization at a dealer.
symptoms: Window rolls up then bounces back down
Window stuck, will not go up or down
Clicking/chattering/grinding from door
Auto-up/one-touch stops working
Glass drops into door

records.title: Shifter Cable Bushing Detaches - Vehicle Rollaway Risk (Recall 18S20 / 22S43)
records.description: A plastic bushing that attaches the shift cable to the transmission can degrade and pop off, so the transmission may be in a different gear than the shift lever indicates. The driver can shift to Park, remove the key, and walk away while the transmission is actually not in Park, allowing the car to roll away. Ford issued recall 18S20 in 2018 (~504,000 vehicles) and later expanded it as 22V413/22S43 after the first repair proved inadequate, adding a protective cap.
records.solution: Under recall (18S20, then 22S43) dealers replace the under-hood shift-cable bushing and install a protective cap at no charge. Owners should always set the parking brake. Out of warranty, the bushing is an inexpensive part but reattaching/replacing it correctly with the cap is essential to prevent recurrence.
symptoms: Vehicle rolls after being placed in Park
Shift lever position does not match actual gear
Difficulty shifting or shifter feels disconnected
Cannot remove key or key removal does not correspond to Park

records.title: Electric Power Steering Rack Failure (Recall 15V340)
records.description: NHTSA recall 15V340 covers 2011-2013 Ford Fusion (and Lincoln MKZ) without the 3.5L engine. An intermittent electrical connection in the steering gear can cause sudden loss of electric power steering assist while driving. Owners notice heavier steering effort especially at low speeds, increasing crash risk. Dealers check the Power Steering Control Module (PSCM) for DTCs; if any loss-of-assist codes are stored, the steering gear is replaced free. Note: 2010 Fusions had the same parts but were excluded from the recall — feds closed the probe without expanding scope. 2010-owner symptoms are real but uncovered by recall.
records.solution: Check if your vehicle is covered under Ford recall (2011-2012 Fusion/MKZ power steering failure recall - free repair). For non-recall vehicles, the electric power steering rack must be replaced as a complete unit since the motor and control electronics are integrated. RepairPal estimates $1,958-3,362 installed. Remanufactured racks from PWR Steer or Cardone are available at $800-1,500, significantly cheaper than new OEM ($2,000+). Have the alignment performed after rack replacement.
symptoms: Power steering warning message on dashboard
Steering becomes heavy or requires extra force
Intermittent loss of power steering assist
Steering wheel off-center after loss of assist
Clunking or grinding from steering column area
Complete loss of power steering (requires significant force to turn)
Steering assist comes and goes unpredictably
Check engine light or power steering fault code stored

records.title: Water Intrusion into Trunk/Tire Well - Wet Carpet and Corroded Modules
records.description: Fusion owners frequently find water pooling in the trunk/spare-tire well and wet rear carpet. Sources include leaking taillight gaskets/plastic rivet pass-throughs, deteriorated trunk and rear-window seals, and split spot-welds in the channel under the rear glass. Standing water risks rust and corrosion of trunk-mounted electronics (on hybrids the high-voltage battery and electronics sit in this area), plus musty odor and mold.
records.solution: Water-test to locate the entry point, then reseal or replace the taillight gaskets/rivet grommets, trunk weatherstrip, and rear-window seal; seal split spot-welds with seam sealer. Clear any blocked trunk/quarter-panel drain holes and dry the carpet/insulation thoroughly to prevent corrosion and mold.
symptoms: Water in spare-tire well
Wet or musty rear carpet
Water dripping near taillights
Foggy/condensation in trunk
Rust or corroded connectors in trunk

records.title: Electric Power Steering Failure — 'Direção Elétrica Avariada' Warning and Sudden Loss of Assist
records.description: Brazilian Ka III owners report a recurring electric power steering (EPS) fault in which assist suddenly cuts out while driving: the steering becomes very heavy, multiple instrument cluster warning lights illuminate, and the message 'Direção elétrica avariada' (electric steering damaged) is displayed. The fault is often intermittent — assist returns after switching the car off and on — and dealers frequently fail to reproduce it or misdiagnose it as a weak battery. Complaint-site records on Reclame Aqui include cases diagnosed as manufacturing defects in the steering rack/column and owners experiencing the failure repeatedly after repairs, including in vehicles still under warranty.
records.solution: Have the EPS system scanned for fault codes and the battery/charging system verified first, since low system voltage can trigger assist cutout. Persistent cases typically require replacement of the electric steering column motor/ECU or the complete steering rack assembly. Document occurrences and pursue warranty or consumer-protection channels for newer vehicles, as the failure mode (loss of assist while moving) is safety-relevant.
symptoms: Steering suddenly becomes very heavy while driving
'Direção elétrica avariada' (electric steering damaged) message on the dash
Multiple warning lights illuminate at the same time
Fault is intermittent — steering works normally after restarting the car
Problem recurs even after dealer repairs or battery replacement

records.title: Oil-Bathed Timing Belt Degradation Causing Oil Starvation (1.0 Ti-VCT 3-Cylinder)
records.description: The Brazilian-built Ka III's 1.0 Ti-VCT three-cylinder engine uses a wet timing belt that runs immersed in engine oil, with a nominal replacement interval of 260,000 km. Brazilian mechanics and the automotive press document a chronic failure pattern: when oil changes are stretched or oil outside Ford's 5W-20 specification is used, the belt's rubber degrades and sheds debris into the sump. The debris clogs the oil pump pickup strainer, causing low oil pressure, hydraulic lifter noise, accelerated wear of bearings and cylinder walls, overheating, and in advanced cases complete engine failure requiring a rebuild. Repair shops report rebuild costs that can approach the market value of the car. The same engine and failure mode also affects the Brazilian EcoSport.
records.solution: Strictly follow oil changes every 10,000 km/6 months with Ford-spec SAE 5W-20 (every 5,000 km/3 months under severe use such as city-only driving). Many Brazilian mechanics recommend replacing the wet belt preventively around 100,000-150,000 km rather than the 260,000 km factory interval. If lifter noise or low oil pressure appears, immediately inspect and clean the oil pump pickup strainer and check for belt debris in the sump; engines run long with a clogged pickup typically need bearing replacement or a full rebuild.
symptoms: Ticking or knocking noise from the engine, especially at cold start
Low oil pressure warning light
Excessive vibration at idle
Rubber or metallic debris found in the oil at oil changes
Engine overheating or loss of power in advanced cases

records.title: Recall: Cracked Driver Airbag Module Mounting Hook in Steering Wheel (2019 Ka Hatch/Sedan)
records.description: In March 2019, Ford Brazil recalled Ka Hatch and Sedan model-year 2019 vehicles manufactured between February 11 and 19, 2019 (chassis range K8293090 to K8327710). During production of the steering wheel frame, a crack may have formed in one of the mounting hooks that secure the driver's airbag module. In a frontal collision that triggers airbag deployment, the damaged module could detach from the steering wheel, compromising airbag function and increasing the risk of injury to occupants. The recall was registered with Procon-SP and publicized by the São Paulo state government.
records.solution: Take the vehicle to a Ford dealership for free inspection and, if necessary, steering wheel replacement. Owners can confirm whether their chassis is affected via Ford Brazil's recall lookup (ford.com.br), the FordPass app, or Ford customer service at 0800 703 3673.
symptoms: No warning signs in normal driving — latent manufacturing defect
Vehicle built between February 11 and 19, 2019, within chassis range K8293090-K8327710
Driver airbag module may detach from the steering wheel during deployment in a frontal crash

citations.title: Procon-SP - Ford Ka Driver-Airbag Mounting Recall

records.title: Recall: Front Seat Recliner Assembled Without Internal Lock (2019-2020 Ka Hatch)
records.description: In September/October 2019, Ford Brazil recalled Ka Hatch model-year 2019 vehicles (manufactured October 10, 2018 to June 1, 2019) and model-year 2020 vehicles (manufactured February 18 to September 19, 2019), together with the EcoSport, because the manual seat-back reclining mechanism of the front seats may have been assembled missing one of its three internal locks. In a rear collision, the absence of one lock can reduce the seat-back's locking force and fail to adequately retain occupants, increasing the risk of injury. Free inspections began October 14, 2019, and the campaign was registered with Procon-SP.
records.solution: Take the vehicle to a Ford dealership for free inspection of both front seat recliner mechanisms and replacement of the recliner assembly if a lock is missing. Check chassis eligibility via Ford Brazil's recall lookup (ford.com.br) or customer service at 0800 703 3673.
symptoms: No symptoms in normal use — defect manifests only in a rear collision
Ka Hatch built between October 2018 and September 2019
Front seat-back may not lock with full force and can give way under rear impact load

citations.title: Ford Brazil - 2019-2020 EcoSport and Ka Seat-Recliner Recall

records.title: DC Fast Charging Faults and Reduced Charging Speed
records.description: Many Ford F-150 Lightning owners report persistent issues with DC fast charging, including charge fault errors, unexpectedly slow charging speeds, and sessions that terminate prematurely. Some vehicles charge at only 40-70kW at stations rated for 150-350kW. The charging speed often drops dramatically after 2-5 minutes at a fast charger, settling well below the advertised 150kW peak rate. The battery charging control module (BCCM) can develop faults that prevent DC fast charging entirely, displaying an orange charge ring and "Vehicle Charging Fault" errors. Ford has released software updates to improve charging performance, but many owners continue to experience issues.
records.solution: Visit the Ford dealer for the latest BCCM and powertrain software updates — Ford has released multiple OTA and dealer-applied updates that improve charging behavior. If charging fault errors persist after software updates, the BCCM may need replacement ($500-$1,500). Try different DC fast charging networks as compatibility varies. Pre-condition the battery by driving for at least 15-20 minutes before DC fast charging in cold weather to improve charging speed. Use the FordPass app to schedule departure time, which pre-conditions the battery.
symptoms: Orange charge indicator ring and "Vehicle Charging Fault" message
DC fast charging speed significantly below advertised peak rate
Charging speed drops dramatically after 2-5 minutes on fast charger
Charge session terminates prematurely before reaching target SOC
Level 2 AC charging works normally but DC fast charging fails
Error messages in FordPass app during charging sessions

records.title: Front Upper Control Arm Ball Joint Separation — Loss of Steering
records.description: Certain 2023-2024 Ford F-150 Lightning trucks were recalled because the front upper control arm ball joint nut may not have been properly tightened during assembly. If the nut loosens, the control arm can separate from the steering knuckle, causing a sudden and complete loss of steering control. This is a manufacturing assembly defect rather than a design flaw, but the consequences are severe — the affected wheel can tuck under the vehicle causing the driver to lose all directional control.
records.solution: Contact your Ford dealer to verify if your vehicle is affected by this recall. The dealer will inspect the front upper control arm ball joint torque specification and re-torque or replace the hardware as needed, free of charge. If you hear clunking from the front end or experience wandering steering, have the vehicle towed to a dealer rather than driving it. Do not drive if you suspect a loose ball joint.
symptoms: Clunking or knocking from the front suspension over bumps
Steering feels loose or wanders at highway speed
Uneven front tire wear
Visible play in the front wheel when lifted off the ground
Sudden loss of steering control (catastrophic failure mode)

records.title: High-Voltage Battery Cell Manufacturing Defect — Internal Short Circuit and Fire Risk
records.description: The Ford F-150 Lightning is under recall (NHTSA 25V131000, Ford 25S18) for a supplier manufacturing defect in the high-voltage battery cells that can cause an internal short circuit. Production process deviations at the battery cell supplier caused misaligned electrodes in some cells. An internal short circuit in the battery pack increases the risk of thermal runaway and fire. Ford is aware of five vehicle fires and one injury claim that may be related. Affected vehicles were built between March 16, 2022 and August 14, 2024. Until the recall is completed, Ford advises owners to charge only to 80% maximum.
records.solution: Contact your Ford dealer immediately to check if your Lightning is affected by recall 25S18 (NHTSA 25V131000). Until the recall is performed, charge the vehicle to a maximum of 80% state of charge. The dealer will inspect the high-voltage battery array and replace it if necessary, free of charge. Park the vehicle outdoors (not in a garage) as a precaution until the inspection is complete. Monitor for any unusual smells, smoke, or heat from the battery area.
symptoms: No symptoms may be present before failure
Unusual heat or warmth from floor/battery area
Burning or chemical smell from under the vehicle
Battery warning messages on the instrument cluster
Reduced range or unexpected battery behavior
Charging faults or errors during charging sessions

citations.title: Ford Recall 25S18 / NHTSA Campaign 25V131 Dealer Notice

records.title: Integrated Park Module Failure — Vehicle May Roll Away When Parked
records.description: The Ford F-150 Lightning has a recall for the integrated park module (IPM) which may fail to lock into the park position when the driver shifts into Park. Unlike conventional vehicles with a mechanical parking pawl connected to the transmission, the Lightning uses an electronic park module. If the module software fails to properly engage the park lock, the vehicle can roll away when the driver exits, increasing the risk of a crash or injury. Ford issued recall 25C69 covering 2022-2025 model year Lightning trucks.
records.solution: Contact your Ford dealer to have the integrated park module software updated under recall 25C69, free of charge. Until the recall is performed, always engage the parking brake manually after shifting to Park as a redundant safety measure. Avoid parking on steep inclines without the parking brake engaged. If the vehicle displays a park system warning or does not show a green "P" indicator when shifted to Park, do not leave the vehicle unattended.
symptoms: Vehicle rolls or creeps after being shifted to Park
Park system warning message on instrument cluster
Green "P" indicator does not display after shifting to Park
Unusual delay when shifting from Drive to Park
Parking brake required to hold vehicle on flat surfaces
