records.title: Catalytic Converter Efficiency Fault (P0420) on 2.5L Duratec
records.description: Transit Connect models with the 2.5L Duratec commonly generate catalyst efficiency codes, often after repeated misfire events, oil consumption, or exhaust leaks upstream of the catalyst. Owners report a persistent check engine light with no drivability change, or reduced power if the catalyst becomes restricted. NHTSA complaints and owner reports frequently cite P0420 and catalytic converter replacement.
records.solution: Diagnose for exhaust leaks, misfires, and fuel trim issues before replacing parts. If confirmed, replace the catalytic converter assembly and address root causes (spark plugs/coils, upstream O2 sensor issues, or oil consumption) to prevent repeat failure.
symptoms: Check engine light on
DTC P0420 stored
Sulfur/rotten egg smell (sometimes)
Reduced power if catalyst is restricted
Failed emissions inspection

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 14V703 - Transit Connect Fuel-Line Routing

records.title: EVAP Purge Valve Stuck Open (Hard Start After Refueling)
records.description: Owners report extended cranking, rough idle, or stalling shortly after refueling due to an EVAP canister purge valve that sticks open and floods the intake with fuel vapor. This failure mode is documented across Ford applications and appears in Transit Connect owner reports and service literature addressing purge valve performance. The condition often triggers EVAP-related DTCs and can worsen over time.
records.solution: Replace the EVAP canister purge valve/solenoid and inspect EVAP lines for liquid fuel contamination. Clear codes and verify proper purge operation with scan tool commands; advise against topping off the tank to reduce recurrence risk.
symptoms: Hard start immediately after refueling
Rough idle or stumble after fill-up
Occasional stall when coming to a stop
Fuel odor near engine bay
Check engine light on

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 15V005 - Transit Connect Fuel Pump

records.title: Front Wheel Bearing/Hubs Premature Wear (Growl/Hum Increases With Speed)
records.description: Transit Connect owners report front hub bearing noise that increases with road speed and changes with steering load, sometimes requiring hub replacement earlier than expected. The vehicle’s duty cycle (commercial use, heavy loads) can accelerate wear, and some reports describe repeated replacements. This issue is commonly documented in owner forums and service histories for Transit Connect vans.
records.solution: Road-test to confirm bearing noise and isolate the affected side; replace the front wheel hub/bearing assembly and torque axle nut to specification. Inspect CV joints and tires for secondary noise sources and verify alignment if uneven tire wear is present.
symptoms: Humming/growling noise that rises with speed
Noise changes when turning left/right
Vibration felt in steering wheel (sometimes)
Uneven tire wear (sometimes)
ABS light if sensor integrated and damaged (rare)

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 21V592 - Transit Connect Passenger Seat Belt

records.title: HVAC Blower Motor Resistor/Control Module Failure (Fan Works Only on High or Not at All)
records.description: Transit Connect owners report the cabin blower losing lower speeds, operating only on high, or stopping entirely due to failure of the blower motor resistor/control module. Heat-related stress and connector resistance can damage the module and/or melt the connector, leading to intermittent operation. This issue is widely documented across Ford platforms and appears in Transit Connect owner reports and service bulletins covering blower control faults.
records.solution: Replace the blower motor resistor/control module and inspect the blower motor for overcurrent draw; replace the blower motor if it draws excessive current. Repair any heat-damaged connector/pigtail and ensure the cabin air filter is not restricted.
symptoms: Blower works only on highest speed
No airflow from vents despite HVAC on
Intermittent blower operation
Burning smell from passenger footwell area
Melted blower resistor connector

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 15V406 - Transit Connect Instrument Cluster

records.title: Ignition Coil Failure and Misfires (2.5L/1.6L)
records.description: Transit Connect owners report intermittent misfires, rough running, and flashing MIL events commonly traced to failing coil-on-plug ignition coils. Heat and age-related breakdown can cause single-cylinder misfires that may damage the catalytic converter if driven long-term. This is frequently documented in owner reports and service records for both the 2.5L Duratec and 1.6L EcoBoost variants.
records.solution: Scan for misfire counters and DTCs, then replace the failed ignition coil(s); replace spark plugs if worn or oil-fouled. If multiple coils show weakness, consider replacing the full set and verify no coolant/oil intrusion into plug wells.
symptoms: Rough idle and hesitation under load
Flashing check engine light during misfire
Loss of power
Poor fuel economy
Sulfur smell or catalyst overheating (if severe)

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 20V305 - Transit Connect Seat-Belt Pretensioners

records.title: PCM Software Calibration Causing Intermittent Stalling
records.description: Multiple 2017-2020 Transit Connect owners report intermittent stalling at idle or during low-speed maneuvers, traced to PCM software calibration issues. The engine drops RPMs erratically and stalls, particularly when the AC compressor engages or when transitioning from reverse to drive. Ford released TSB 19-2346 addressing this with an updated PCM calibration, but many vehicles remain unflashed.
records.solution: Dealer PCM reflash/recalibration per Ford TSB 19-2346. The updated calibration adjusts idle air control parameters and torque converter clutch engagement logic. If stalling persists after reflash, inspect the throttle body for carbon buildup and clean with CRC throttle body cleaner. A failing throttle position sensor can produce similar symptoms and should be ruled out.
symptoms: Engine stalls at idle, especially in drive with foot on brake
RPM drops below 500 then recovers or stalls
Stalling when shifting from reverse to drive
Stalling when AC compressor kicks on
Check engine light with idle-related codes

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 25V196 - Transit Connect PCM Cooling Thresholds

records.title: Electric Power Steering Assist Motor Failure
records.description: The Transit Connect uses an electric power steering (EPAS) system with a column-mounted assist motor that is prone to failure between 60,000-100,000 miles. Symptoms range from intermittent loss of power assist to complete failure requiring significant steering effort. The steering warning light illuminates and the system may enter a reduced-assist mode. Failures are more common in vehicles used for delivery routes with frequent low-speed turning.
records.solution: Replace the electric power steering motor/torque sensor assembly. Ford part DT1Z-3504-C covers most model years. The steering column does not need removal in most cases — the motor unbolt from the column. After replacement, a steering angle sensor calibration must be performed with a Ford IDS or compatible scan tool. Used/remanufactured EPAS motors from reputable rebuilders can save 40-60% over new OEM.
symptoms: Power steering warning light on dashboard
Intermittent heavy steering, especially at low speeds
Complete loss of power steering assist
Steering assist cuts in and out randomly
Whining or grinding noise from steering column area

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 22V192 - Transit Connect Windshield Adhesion

records.title: Rear Door Wiring Harness Break (Liftgate/Rear Electrical Intermittent)
records.description: Repeated opening/closing of the liftgate can fatigue and break wires in the rubber boot/harness at the rear hinge area. Owners report intermittent rear wiper, rear defrost, license plate lamps, rear camera, and/or liftgate release issues that come and go with liftgate movement. This pattern is documented in owner reports and NHTSA complaints describing intermittent rear electrical faults tied to harness flexing.
records.solution: Pull back the hinge/boot and perform a continuity test on suspect circuits; repair broken conductors with solder/heat-shrink or replace the rear liftgate harness section. Secure routing to reduce strain and verify all rear functions after repair.
symptoms: Rear wiper inoperative or intermittent
Backup camera cuts out intermittently
License plate lamps flicker or fail
Liftgate release works only sometimes
Problems change when liftgate is moved

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 25V442 - Transit Connect Rearview-Camera Software

records.title: Rear Liftgate Latch/Handle Failure (Liftgate Won’t Open)
records.description: Owners report the rear liftgate handle/latch mechanism binding or failing, leaving the liftgate stuck closed or intermittently not releasing. Complaints commonly describe the exterior handle feeling loose or the latch motor/actuator not responding, sometimes after water intrusion or wear in the latch assembly. This is frequently documented in owner reports and NHTSA complaints for Transit Connect wagons.
records.solution: Inspect liftgate handle and latch for broken linkage and water intrusion; replace the liftgate latch/actuator assembly and/or exterior handle as needed. Verify wiring at the liftgate harness and confirm latch operation with scan tool output tests if equipped.
symptoms: Liftgate will not open with exterior handle
Intermittent latch release; requires repeated attempts
Handle feels loose or has no resistance
Rear cargo access blocked
Latch works only with key fob or only from inside (if equipped)

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 23V502 - Transit Connect Front Door Latches

records.title: Rear Suspension Clunking Over Bumps — Stabilizer Bar Links and Bushings
records.description: The Transit Connect rear suspension develops a persistent clunking or knocking noise over bumps, particularly noticeable at low speeds in parking lots and over speed bumps. The primary cause is worn rear stabilizer bar end links and bushings, though rear shock absorber upper mounts also fail prematurely. Loaded commercial vehicles that regularly carry cargo accelerate wear significantly. The issue typically presents between 40,000-70,000 miles.
records.solution: Replace rear stabilizer bar end links (both sides) and stabilizer bar bushings as a set. Inspect rear shock absorber upper mounts for cracking or separation — replace shocks if mounts are compromised. Moog K750612 end links and Energy Suspension polyurethane bushings are popular upgrades over OEM rubber. Torque all fasteners to spec: end link nuts to 46 ft-lbs, bushing bracket bolts to 35 ft-lbs.
symptoms: Clunking or knocking from rear over bumps
Rattling noise on rough roads
Loose feeling in rear end during turns
Noise worsens with cargo load
Visible play in stabilizer bar links when inspected

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 20V550 - Transit Connect Start/Stop Accumulator

records.title: Sliding Door Cable and Roller Mechanism Failure
records.description: The second-generation Ford Transit Connect (2014+) suffers from premature failure of the sliding door cable and roller mechanism on both driver and passenger sides. The cable frays or snaps, and the nylon rollers crack or wear flat, causing the door to bind, jump off the track, or refuse to open/close fully. This is especially common in commercial-use vehicles that see 20-50+ door cycles per day.
records.solution: Replace the complete sliding door cable and roller assembly (Ford part 9T1Z-16A506-A or equivalent). Both the upper and lower roller assemblies should be replaced together. Lubricate the track rail with white lithium grease every 6 months for commercial use. Some owners upgrade to aftermarket stainless steel roller kits for improved durability.
symptoms: Sliding door sticks or binds when opening/closing
Door jumps off track partially
Grinding or scraping noise when operating door
Door will not latch fully closed
Visible frayed cable near door hinge area

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 14V777 - Transit Connect Sliding-Door Panel

records.title: Water Leak Through Taillight Housing Gasket
records.description: The Transit Connect taillight housing gaskets deteriorate and allow water intrusion into the rear cargo area, particularly on the passenger side. Water pools in the spare tire well and behind interior panels, causing mold, corrosion of wiring harnesses, and eventual electrical gremlins including inoperative taillights and backup camera failures. The issue is worsened by car wash pressure or heavy rain.
records.solution: Remove both taillight assemblies and replace the foam gaskets with new Ford OEM gaskets or high-quality butyl tape sealant. Clean all mating surfaces thoroughly before resealing. Inspect and dry out the spare tire well and wiring harness connectors for corrosion. Apply dielectric grease to all electrical connectors in the affected area. Check and clear the rear body drain plugs which often clog with debris.
symptoms: Water pooling in spare tire well or rear cargo area
Musty or mold smell from rear of vehicle
Intermittent taillight or backup camera failure
Visible moisture or fogging inside taillight lens
Corrosion on rear wiring connectors

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 25V572 - Transit Connect Rearview Camera

records.title: Throttle Body/ETC Fault Causing Limp Mode (Reduced Engine Power)
records.description: Owners report sudden reduced power, poor throttle response, and limp-home behavior due to electronic throttle body contamination/wear or throttle actuator control faults. The issue can be intermittent and may clear after a key cycle, then recur, which is a common pattern in NHTSA complaints and owner reports. It often sets throttle/ETC-related DTCs and can be triggered by carbon buildup or failing throttle position sensing.
records.solution: Confirm DTCs and perform throttle body inspection/cleaning if contamination is present; if faults persist, replace the throttle body assembly and perform the required idle/throttle relearn procedure. Inspect related wiring/connectors and verify PCM updates if applicable.
symptoms: Reduced engine power message/limp mode
Poor throttle response or no acceleration
Stalling or near-stalling at idle
Intermittent issue resolved by key cycle
Check engine light on

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 22V413 - Transit Connect Shifter-Cable Bushing

records.title: Cooling System Degas Bottle (Coolant Reservoir) Cracking/Leak Leading to Overheating
records.description: NHTSA complaints and owner reports describe coolant loss from the plastic degas bottle/reservoir cracking or leaking at seams, causing low coolant warnings and overheating if not caught early. Heat cycling and plastic aging can lead to hairline cracks that only leak under pressure. Drivers often notice a sweet smell, visible coolant residue, or repeated low coolant level.
records.solution: Pressure-test the cooling system and replace the degas bottle/reservoir and cap if leaking; refill with the correct Motorcraft coolant and bleed air per Ford procedure. Inspect hoses and the thermostat housing area for secondary leaks and verify fan operation.
symptoms: Low coolant level / repeated top-offs
Coolant smell in engine bay
Visible coolant residue around reservoir
Engine temperature rises/overheating
Heater performance fluctuates due to air in system

records.title: Driveshaft Center Support / Carrier Bearing Failure
records.description: Long-wheelbase and extended-length Transit models (T-250, T-350, T-350 HD) with two-piece driveshafts develop carrier bearing (center support bearing) failure. The rubber isolator deteriorates and the bearing wears, causing vibrations at highway speeds (50-70 mph) and a prominent clunking noise when shifting between drive and reverse. The issue is accelerated by frequent payload at or near GVWR. The vibration is often misdiagnosed as a tire balance issue.
records.solution: Replace the driveshaft center support bearing assembly (carrier bearing, rubber mount, and bracket as a unit). Ford part CK4Z-4R602-D for long-wheelbase models. The driveshaft must be properly phased during reinstallation — mark both halves and the carrier bearing bracket position before removal. Failure to maintain proper phasing causes NVH issues. Torque the carrier bearing bracket bolts to 52 ft-lbs.
symptoms: Vibration at highway speeds (50-70 mph)
Clunk when shifting from drive to reverse
Rumbling or grinding noise from under vehicle
Vibration worsens under load
Visible rubber deterioration on center bearing mount

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 19V767 - Transit Driveshaft Flexible Coupling

records.title: Electric Power Steering (EPAS) Assist Loss / Steering Fault Warnings
records.description: NHTSA complaints include intermittent or sudden loss of power steering assist with warning messages, making the van difficult to steer at low speeds. Reports often describe the issue occurring after a restart, during parking maneuvers, or intermittently with electrical/communication faults. The Transit’s EPAS system can set steering-related DTCs and may require module diagnosis or replacement depending on root cause.
records.solution: Scan for PSCM/ABS network faults, check battery/charging health and grounds, inspect steering rack electrical connections, and update software if applicable. If confirmed, replace the steering gear/EPAS rack or related control module per Ford diagnostics and perform steering angle/center calibration.
symptoms: Power steering assist reduced or lost
Steering warning light/message
Heavy steering at low speeds
Intermittent return of assist after key cycle
Steering-related communication faults

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 24V542 - Transit Trail EPAS Ground

records.title: Front Brake Caliper Sticking / Premature Pad and Rotor Wear
records.description: Front brake calipers on the Ford Transit, especially the heavy-duty variants (350 and 350HD), are prone to sticking due to corrosion of the caliper slide pins and guide bolts. The high gross vehicle weight combined with stop-and-go commercial use accelerates heat buildup, which bakes the slide pin grease and causes the pins to seize. This results in one pad wearing far faster than the other, warped rotors, and a persistent pulling sensation during braking. NHTSA has received numerous complaints on this issue across 2015–2022 model years.
records.solution: Remove front calipers and thoroughly clean and re-lubricate or replace slide pins using high-temperature caliper grease (Motorcraft XG-3 or equivalent). Replace worn pads and rotors as a set. In severe seizure cases, replace the entire caliper assembly (Motorcraft BICF-141 or equivalent). Inspect and replace rubber slide pin boots if cracked or torn.
symptoms: Vehicle pulling to one side during braking
Premature or uneven pad and rotor wear on one side
Burning smell from front wheel area after driving
Brake drag or reduced fuel economy
Squealing or grinding noise from front brakes at low mileage

records.title: Front Suspension Radius Arm Bushing Premature Wear and Cracking
records.description: The Ford Transit uses a twin I-beam or independent front suspension with radius arm bushings that are known to wear or crack prematurely, especially in high-mileage commercial fleets or when the vehicle is operated at or near maximum payload regularly. Worn bushings cause the front axle geometry to shift, leading to rapid and uneven tire wear, vague steering, and a pronounced clunking noise over bumps. This is a documented issue in NHTSA complaints and Transit owner forums, particularly on 2015–2020 models used for delivery service.
records.solution: Replace front radius arm bushings. OEM Ford bushing kit (part number BK3Z-3B203-A or updated revision) should be used. Some owners opt for aftermarket polyurethane bushing upgrades (e.g., Energy Suspension kits) for improved durability. Labor typically involves pressing old bushings out and pressing new ones in with a hydraulic press.
symptoms: Clunking or banging noise from front suspension over bumps
Rapid or uneven front tire wear
Vague or wandering steering feel
Visible cracking or deformation of rubber bushing material
Vehicle pulling to one side during braking

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 21V324 - Transit Rear Wheel Studs

records.title: Fuel Injector Failure and Rough Running (EcoBlue Diesel)
records.description: The 2017-2023 Ford Transit with the 2.0L EcoBlue diesel engine (available in some markets) and the 3.5L EcoBoost V6 experience fuel injector failures causing rough running, misfires, poor idle, reduced performance, and excessive smoke on cold start. Parkers UK documents an official Ford service action for Transit EcoBlue diesel injector failures traced to a quality issue with Continental-supplied injectors where an internal surface coating comes unstuck, blocking the injector. FordTransitUSAForum.com documents injector failure on 3.5L EcoBoost Transit models as well, where direct injection fuel deposits cause injector spray pattern degradation. RepairPal estimates individual injector replacement between $266 and $627 depending on Transit model, but multiple injectors often need replacement simultaneously, and contaminated fuel systems can cost significantly more.
records.solution: For Transit 3.5L EcoBoost: replace failed injectors ($100-200 per injector, 3-4 hours labor). Consider replacing all 6 injectors if the vehicle has over 100k miles - if one has failed, others are likely close behind. For EcoBlue diesel: Ford issued a service action for Continental injector failures - check with dealer for coverage. Use only Top Tier gasoline and change fuel filters per schedule. Professional fuel system cleaning every 50,000 miles can extend injector life.
symptoms: Rough running and engine misfires
Poor idle quality
Excessive blue or black smoke on cold start
Reduced engine performance and power
Check engine light with injector or misfire codes
Engine stalls immediately after starting
High fuel consumption
Engine hesitation under acceleration

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 16V618 - Transit 3.2L Diesel Fuel System

records.title: Instrument Cluster / Speedometer Erratic Readings and Gauge Dropout
records.description: Multiple Ford Transit owners and fleet operators have reported the instrument cluster exhibiting erratic speedometer behavior, gauge dropouts, and spontaneous warning light illumination without stored fault codes corresponding to the indicated faults. The issue is linked to a faulty instrument cluster circuit board or intermittent loss of communication between the cluster and the vehicle's CAN bus network. Ford issued TSB 20-2253 related to instrument cluster display concerns on 2020–2021 Transit models, and earlier model years have similar complaints documented in NHTSA's database.
records.solution: Diagnose CAN bus communication using Ford IDS/FDRS to identify any U-code network faults. Inspect cluster connector pins for corrosion or pushed-back terminals. In confirmed cluster failure cases, replace the instrument cluster assembly (Ford part number varies by configuration and trim; must be programmed to vehicle VIN). TSB 20-2253 recommends module reprogramming as a first step before hardware replacement.
symptoms: Speedometer needle sweeping erratically or reading zero while moving
Warning lights (ABS, airbag, check engine) illuminating and extinguishing randomly
Fuel gauge or temperature gauge showing incorrect readings
Total cluster blackout while driving
U-code network communication fault codes stored

records.title: NOx Sensor / SCR DEF System Faults Causing Reduced Power (2.0L EcoBlue Diesel)
records.description: EcoBlue diesel Transits have documented owner reports of check engine lights and emissions system warnings related to SCR/DEF operation, commonly tied to NOx sensor faults or SCR efficiency monitoring. When the system detects persistent faults, it may trigger reduced power or countdown-to-no-start strategies depending on market/calibration. These issues are frequently accompanied by emissions-related DTCs and can be intermittent before becoming persistent.
records.solution: Diagnose SCR system with a capable scan tool, verify DEF quality, check wiring/connectors at NOx sensors, and replace failed NOx sensor(s) as indicated; perform required resets/adaptations. If applicable per Ford service guidance, update PCM calibration addressing false SCR/NOx diagnostics and confirm proper dosing operation.
symptoms: Check engine light with emissions warnings
Reduced power / limp mode
DEF/SCR warning messages
Increased DEF consumption or abnormal dosing behavior
Potential countdown-to-no-start (market dependent)

records.title: Oil Pan Drain Plug Thread Stripping
records.description: The Ford Transit aluminum oil pan is prone to drain plug thread stripping, especially in vehicles serviced at quick-lube shops or with frequent oil changes. The aluminum pan threads are softer than the steel drain plug, and over-torquing or cross-threading during routine oil changes permanently damages the threads. Once stripped, the drain plug leaks oil or falls out entirely, potentially causing catastrophic engine damage from oil starvation.
records.solution: For minor thread damage: install a Time-Sert or Helicoil thread repair insert (M14x1.5 for most Transit models). This is a permanent repair that is actually stronger than the original threads. For severe damage: replace the oil pan ($200-400 for the pan plus 2-3 hours labor). Prevent recurrence by always hand-threading the drain plug first, then torquing to exactly 20 ft-lbs (not more). Use a new crush washer at every oil change.
symptoms: Oil dripping from drain plug area after oil change
Drain plug feels loose or wobbles
Oil spots on ground under engine
Low oil pressure warning after recent service
Drain plug cannot be tightened properly

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 25V344 - Transit Connecting Rods and Bearings

records.title: PCM/ECM Software Calibration Causing Stall or No-Start After Refueling
records.description: Ford Transit owners, particularly those with the 3.5L EcoBoost and 3.7L V6, have reported stalling or no-start conditions immediately after refueling due to fuel vapor purge system calibration issues within the PCM. The evaporative emission canister purge valve and PCM calibration can cause an overly rich condition when the purge valve opens after a full fill-up, flooding the intake and stalling the engine. Ford issued TSB 21-2299 addressing PCM reprogramming to correct the purge flow logic.
records.solution: Reprogram the PCM/ECM with updated Ford calibration per TSB 21-2299. In some cases, the EVAP canister purge valve (Motorcraft CM-5085 or equivalent) also requires replacement. Dealer scan tool (IDS/FDRS) is required for the reflash procedure.
symptoms: Engine stalls immediately after filling fuel tank
Hard start or no-start condition after refueling
Strong fuel smell from engine bay after fill-up
Rough idle following fueling event
P0441 or P0443 EVAP-related codes stored

records.title: Rear Axle Oil Seal Leak at Axle Shaft
records.description: The Ford Transit rear-wheel-drive models develop axle shaft oil seal leaks at the rear differential, allowing gear oil to weep past the axle seals onto the brake backing plates and brake shoes/pads. The leak is often slow enough to go unnoticed until a rear brake inspection reveals oil-soaked components. In severe cases, contaminated rear brakes cause pulling to one side under braking, which is a significant safety concern for loaded vans.
records.solution: Replace the rear axle shaft oil seals (both sides recommended even if only one is leaking). Remove the axle shaft, clean the axle tube bore, and install new seals using a seal driver to ensure proper depth. Inspect rear brake shoes/pads and drums/rotors for oil contamination — replace if soaked. Top off the differential with 75W-140 synthetic gear oil to the fill plug level. Check the differential vent hose for blockage, which causes internal pressure buildup and accelerates seal failure.
symptoms: Oil residue visible on inside of rear wheels
Rear brakes feel spongy or pull to one side
Gear oil smell near rear axle
Oil spots on brake backing plate
Low rear differential fluid level

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 24V805 - Transit Rear-Axle Shaft Bolts

records.title: Rear HVAC Line/Expansion Valve Leaks (Dual A/C) Causing Loss of Refrigerant
records.description: Transits equipped with rear A/C (dual HVAC) have documented complaints of repeated refrigerant loss and poor cooling, often traced to leaks at rear A/C lines, fittings, or rear expansion valve connections. Corrosion, vibration, and seal degradation can lead to slow leaks that are hard to find without dye or electronic leak detection. Owners typically notice rear cooling performance dropping first, then the entire system stops cooling.
records.solution: Leak-test the system, repair/replace leaking rear A/C lines or rear expansion valve seals/components as needed, then evacuate and recharge to specification. Replace any corroded line sections and install updated seals where applicable; verify condenser fan operation and system pressures after repair.
symptoms: Rear A/C warm while front still cool
A/C stops cooling entirely over time
Hissing near rear HVAC unit or lines
Oily residue at A/C fittings/lines
Repeated need for refrigerant recharge

records.title: Rear Leaf Spring U-Bolt and Spring Pack Fatigue / Breakage
records.description: Ford Transit rear leaf springs and their associated U-bolts have been reported to crack, fatigue, or break outright on high-roof and extended-length variants that are operated at or near maximum payload, particularly in commercial fleet service. The high static load combined with road impacts can cause individual spring leaves to crack and the U-bolts clamping the spring to the axle to loosen or fracture. This is noted in multiple NHTSA complaints and fleet maintenance records as a recurring maintenance item on work vans with 150,000+ miles.
records.solution: Inspect rear leaf spring assemblies and U-bolts during every major service interval on loaded vehicles. Replace cracked or fatigued spring leaves with OEM Ford spring assemblies or heavy-duty aftermarket equivalents (e.g., Deaver or National Spring). Replace U-bolts (Ford part number KK3Z-5586-A) whenever springs are disturbed. Torque U-bolt nuts to Ford specification (typically 129–174 Nm depending on variant).
symptoms: Audible clunking or banging from rear axle area under load
Vehicle sits noticeably lower on one side at rear
Visible crack or separation in leaf spring pack
Rear axle shifts laterally under hard acceleration or braking
Vibration felt through floor at highway speeds when loaded

records.title: Roof Water Leaks and Premature Rust - All Body Styles
records.description: Ford Transit vans are well-known for water infiltration through the roof, particularly in medium-roof and high-roof configurations. Water intrudes through multiple paths: (1) factory roof plug holes (the 2015 roof has 16 plugged holes for optional roof rack and ancillary hardware), (2) roof rack mounting holes where Ford applies only primer circles without top-coat paint, (3) push-pin trim clips along the roof/wall junction, and (4) blocked windshield gutter channels that direct water into the engine bay instead of away from the vehicle. The rust issue is compounded by thin steel roofs and inadequate factory corrosion protection. The FordTransitUSAForum has extensive documentation of roof rust appearing within 3-5 years on vans operating in salt-belt states (Northeast, Midwest). For conversion van owners, water leaks can ruin expensive interior buildouts.
records.solution: Preventive sealing: seal all roof plug holes with Dicor lap sealant or Eternabond RV roof tape immediately after purchase. Clean and seal all roof rack mounting holes with rust-inhibiting primer and clear coat. Inspect and clear windshield gutter drains annually. Apply rust-inhibiting undercoat to roof panel interior annually in salt-belt climates. For existing rust: wire brush, treat with Rust-Oleum Rust Reformer, apply self-etching primer, then paint. Dicor 501LSW or Eternabond tape are the most popular roof repair products among Transit owners.
symptoms: Water inside cargo area after rain, especially at roof/wall junction
Water in cab during heavy rain
Rust bubbles or surface rust appearing on roof panel
Water stains on headliner or cargo area ceiling
Wet floor mats from water entering through gutter area
Musty smell inside van
Water in engine compartment during rain (blocked windshield gutters)

records.title: Sliding Door Track/Roller Wear Causing Binding, Noise, or Door Not Closing
records.description: NHTSA complaints and fleet/owner reports commonly cite the Transit sliding door becoming difficult to open/close, popping, grinding, or failing to latch. Wear in the center roller/hinge and track hardware can cause misalignment, especially on high-use cargo vans. The problem often worsens over time and can lead to the door not fully closing or reopening after latching.
records.solution: Inspect and replace worn center roller/hinge assemblies and damaged track components; realign the sliding door per Ford body service procedure and lubricate tracks with the specified lubricant. Replace any bent track brackets and verify latch operation and striker alignment.
symptoms: Sliding door binds or requires excessive force
Grinding/popping noise from door track
Door won’t latch or reopens after closing
Visible sag/misalignment at rear of sliding door
Uneven door gaps

records.title: Turbo Wastegate Actuator Sticking Causing Limp Mode
records.description: The 3.5L EcoBoost twin-turbo Transit models experience wastegate actuator sticking, particularly on the passenger-side turbo. Carbon buildup and heat cycling cause the wastegate pivot to seize, resulting in either overboosting (wastegate stuck closed) or underboosting (stuck open). Overboosting triggers an immediate limp mode with reduced power. The issue is more prevalent in Transit vans used for towing or heavy cargo loads that keep the turbos under sustained high heat.
records.solution: First attempt: remove the wastegate actuator arm and clean the pivot with PB Blaster, then exercise it through full range of motion. Apply high-temp anti-seize to the pivot. If the pivot is corroded beyond cleaning, replace the wastegate actuator assembly ($200-400 per side). In severe cases, the entire turbocharger must be replaced. Preventive maintenance: exercise the wastegate linkage every oil change and avoid extended idle periods that promote carbon buildup.
symptoms: Limp mode / reduced engine power warning
Check engine light with boost-related codes
Turbo whistle or flutter noise changes character
Loss of power under acceleration
Audible metallic rattle from turbo area at idle

records.title: Turbocharger Boost Pressure Sensor / MAP Sensor Failure (2.0L EcoBlue)
records.description: The 2.0L EcoBlue diesel Transit has a documented pattern of boost pressure sensor and manifold absolute pressure (MAP) sensor failures, causing incorrect boost readings fed to the ECM. When the sensor fails or reads out of range, the ECM defaults to a conservative fueling map, reducing power significantly and triggering a check engine light. This issue is noted in multiple European market TSBs and has been replicated in North American Transit owners' forums with the same engine.
records.solution: Replace the boost pressure/MAP sensor located on the intake manifold. Ford part number for the 2.0L EcoBlue MAP sensor is approximately 2 235 233 (or Motorcraft DY-1297). Clearing the fault and re-testing boost response is required after replacement. ECM recalibration via Ford FDRS may be needed if a learned adaptation table has been skewed by the faulty sensor data.
symptoms: Noticeable reduction in engine power or sluggish acceleration
Check engine light with boost-related fault codes
Excessive black smoke from exhaust under load
Turbo appears to not build boost pressure
Poor fuel economy compared to baseline

records.title: 1.6L EcoBoost Engine Overheating and Coolant Loss - Recall 14S11
records.description: The 1.6L EcoBoost engine in 2014-2018 Ford Transit Connect has documented issues with coolant loss, overheating, and in severe cases engine fires. Ford issued Recall 14S11 (NHTSA 14V309) for 2013-2014 models covering coolant leakage from the cylinder head that could contact hot engine components and cause fire. The 1.6L EcoBoost was also susceptible to head gasket failure and internal coolant leaks similar to the 1.5L and 2.0L EcoBoost engines in other Ford models. The engine was discontinued and replaced by the 2.0L EcoBoost in later Transit Connect models. The FordTransitConnectForum documents numerous cases of premature engine failure on 1.6L-equipped vans used in commercial service.
records.solution: Check safercar.gov for Recall 14V309/14S11 coverage. Dealers replace coolant hose and associated components under recall. For post-recall coolant issues: cylinder head inspection and replacement of head gasket if internal coolant leak is confirmed. Extended warranty coverage varies - contact Ford Customer Relations. For commercial operators: consider replacing the 1.6L EcoBoost with the 2.5L i-VCT engine from later Transit Connect models if available.
symptoms: Coolant loss without visible external leak
Engine overheating warning
White smoke from exhaust
Sweet smell from engine bay
Check engine light
Engine rough running or misfires
Smoke or fire from engine compartment (severe cases)

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 17V209 - Transit Connect 1.6L GTDI Cooling

records.title: 8F35 8-Speed Automatic Transmission Shudder and Failure
records.description: The 2019-2023 Ford Transit Connect equipped with the 8F35 8-speed automatic transmission experiences transmission shuddering, harsh engagements, slipping, and premature failure. Ford issued a Technical Service Bulletin for 2019-2021 Transit Connect vehicles built before December 20, 2021 with the 8F35 transmission addressing slipping and harsh engagement concerns. FordTransitUSAForum.com documents a 2019 Transit Connect XL 8F35 transmission failure at the 75,000 mile mark. Eng-Tips.com engineering forums discuss the inherent shudder issue in the 8F35 torque converter clutch. Earlier Transit Connect models with the 6F35 transmission also had recall campaigns (2013-2021 models). The transmission issues are exacerbated by commercial use patterns - frequent stops, loaded cargo, and city driving accelerate wear on the torque converter clutch and internal clutch packs.
records.solution: First step: check for TSB coverage and have the dealer perform a transmission fluid change with genuine Motorcraft Mercon ULV fluid and a TCM software recalibration. For 2019-2021 Transit Connect built before 12/20/2021, Ford TSB addresses 8F35 slipping. If shudder persists after fluid change and reprogram, the torque converter may need replacement ($800-1,500). Complete transmission replacement for internal failure runs $3,000-4,500. The powertrain warranty (5yr/60k miles) should cover this on newer vehicles.
symptoms: Shuddering during light acceleration at 25-45 mph
Harsh or jerky gear shifts
Delayed engagement from Park to Drive
Transmission slipping under load
Check engine light with transmission codes
Transmission warning message on dashboard
Grinding or whining noise from transmission
Vehicle hesitates or surges at low speed

citations.title: Ford TSB 23-2333 - Transit Connect 8F35 Slipping and Harsh Engagement

records.title: Side Door Latch Failure - Door May Open While Driving (Recall 16S30)
records.description: The 2014-2016 Ford Transit Connect was included in one of Ford's largest-ever recalls affecting over 2 million vehicles for defective side door latches. NHTSA Campaign Number 16V643 covers approximately 112,225 Transit Connect vehicles manufactured between August 9, 2013 and February 1, 2016. The C1A door latch contains a pawl spring tab that is susceptible to cracking and fracture after repeated exposure to high temperatures and normal cycling. A broken spring tab may prevent the door from latching securely or cause a latched door to unlatch while driving. Consumer Reports reported on the massive Ford and Lincoln recall to fix door latches, and NHTSA documented the safety risk of doors opening while the vehicle is in motion. Ford also issued recall 20S30 and 23S36 for additional door latch concerns on overlapping model years.
records.solution: This is a safety recall - repairs are FREE at any Ford dealer regardless of mileage, ownership status, or warranty coverage. Contact Ford at 1-866-436-7332 or check safercar.gov with your VIN. Ford recall numbers: 16S30, 20S30, 23S36. NHTSA campaign numbers: 16V643, additional campaigns may apply. Dealers replace all affected door latches with improved design parts. If you purchased the vehicle used, the recall still applies - check immediately.
symptoms: Door does not latch securely when closed
Door ajar warning light stays on
Door opens unexpectedly while driving
Door requires extra force to close properly
Clicking or unusual noise from door latch mechanism
Interior dome light stays on indicating door is ajar

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 16V643 - Transit Connect Door Latches
NHTSA Campaign 20V331 - Transit Connect Door-Latch Re-Inspection

records.title: 3.8L V6 Head Gasket Failure
records.description: The 3.8L Essex V6 in the Windstar is notorious for head gasket failure, often caused by the aluminum heads warping from overheating. The composite head gaskets deteriorate and allow coolant into combustion chambers.
records.solution: Confirm head gasket failure with a cooling-system pressure test, combustion-gas/block test, compression or leak-down test, and inspection for coolant in the oil or steam-cleaned spark plugs. Repair requires removing both cylinder heads, checking the heads and block for warpage/cracks, machining or replacing warped heads, and installing updated head gaskets with new torque-to-yield head bolts; the cooling system should also be flushed and the thermostat, radiator cap, and any overheating-related components replaced as needed. Because overheating commonly triggers the failure, inspect the water pump, radiator, fans, and intake manifold sealing before reassembly. Typical repair cost is about $1,500-$3,000 depending on machine-shop work and whether engine damage has occurred.
symptoms: White exhaust smoke
Coolant loss
Overheating
Milky oil

records.title: Intake Manifold Gasket Coolant Leak
records.description: The 3.8L V6 intake manifold gaskets degrade and allow coolant to leak externally or internally into the engine oil. This is closely related to the head gasket issue and can lead to overheating and engine damage if not addressed.
records.solution: Replace both upper and lower intake manifold gaskets. Use updated Fel-Pro gaskets. Flush the cooling system and change the oil if coolant contamination is found.
symptoms: Coolant loss with no visible leak
Milky oil
Overheating
Coolant smell from engine bay

records.title: Power Window Motor and Regulator Failure
records.description: Power window motors and regulators fail frequently, especially on the driver's side. The plastic guide clips break, causing the window to drop into the door or operate very slowly.
records.solution: Replace the window regulator and motor as an assembly. Aftermarket units are widely available and more cost-effective than OEM.
symptoms: Window drops into door
Slow window operation
Grinding noise
Window won't stay up

records.title: Rear Axle Breakage (Safety Recall)
records.description: The Windstar rear axle is prone to stress fracture and complete breakage at the spring perch, causing the wheel to tuck under the vehicle. This was subject to NHTSA recall 10V-040. Rust and corrosion in northern climates accelerates the failure.
records.solution: Inspect the rear beam axle closely at both spring seats/perches and trailing arm attachment areas for perforation, heavy scaling, or cracks; if any corrosion damage is present, the axle should not be welded for repair and must be replaced. Ford’s recall remedy for affected 1998-2003 Windstar vans was installation of reinforcement brackets if the axle passed inspection, or complete rear axle assembly replacement if cracking or severe corrosion was found, followed by a rear alignment check and inspection of shocks, brake hoses, and rear tires for collateral damage. If the recall is still open, the repair may be performed at no charge by a Ford dealer; outside recall coverage, typical owner-pay cost for a complete rear axle replacement is about $1,200-$2,500 depending on parts availability, rust severity, and labor.
symptoms: Clunking from rear
Rear end sway
Visible rust/cracking on rear axle
Uneven tire wear

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 10V385 - Windstar Rear Axle Corrosion

records.title: AX4S/AX4N Automatic Transmission Failure
records.description: The Ford Windstar equipped with the AX4S (1995-2000) and AX4N/4F50N (2001-2003) automatic transmissions suffers from widespread premature transmission failure. CarComplaints.com records 140 complaints for the 2000 model year alone, and 166 problems for the 2003 model year, making transmission failure the single most reported problem for the Windstar. The AX family of transmissions in the Windstar struggles with lubrication problems, harsh 1-2 and 2-1 gear changes, torque converter clutch issues, and catastrophic internal failures. The torque converter clutch solenoid is a particularly weak point, causing shuddering and codes P0741 and P1744. Average repair cost is $2,190 at 102,200 miles according to CarComplaints.com data. Many owners report needing a complete transmission replacement or rebuild, with costs ranging from $1,750 to $3,100.
records.solution: For TCC shudder only (codes P0741/P1744), start with transmission fluid change and TCC solenoid replacement ($400-800). For complete transmission failure, remanufactured transmission replacement is the most common solution ($1,750-2,500 installed). Jasper and Ford Motorcraft remanufactured units are the most commonly recommended. Rebuild is an option at $2,000-3,100 but ensure the torque converter is also replaced. Preventive: change transmission fluid every 30,000 miles - the Windstar transmission runs hot and degrades fluid rapidly.
symptoms: Harsh or jerky 1-2 and 2-1 gear shifts
Transmission slipping or shuddering during acceleration
Torque converter shudder at 40-55 mph
Check engine light with transmission codes
Delayed engagement when shifting from Park to Drive
Transmission overheating warning
Complete loss of forward gears
Grinding or whining noise from transmission

citations.title: NHTSA Campaign 97V097 - Windstar AX4S Servo Cover
